prompt: A network technician replaced an access layer switch and needs to reconfigure it to allow the connected devices to connect to the correct networks.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on the appropriate port(s) on Switch 1 and Switch 3 to verify or reconfigure the correct settings:
Ensure each device accesses only its correctly associated network.
Disable all unused switchports.
Require fault-tolerant connections between the switches.
Only make necessary changes to complete the above requirements.
summary: Inspect and correct the port settings on Switch 1 and Switch 3 so each attached device reaches only its own VLAN, unused ports are shut down, and the inter-switch links are fault tolerant.

pairs.match: Set VLANs to match the attached devices only (e.g., server ports carry VLAN 90, tagged where required)
Ensure unused VLANs are not active or set to untagged on these ports
Align with connected devices; if it connects to printers, VLAN 60 tagged and all other VLANs disabled or untagged
Enable only VLANs relevant to the connected devices (e.g., VLAN 150 for WLAN mobile users), tagged or untagged per policy
Disable any VLAN not associated with the connected devices
Configure LACP on the multiple ports joining the switches
Set duplex to Auto to avoid duplex mismatch
Disable any port that is not connected or planned for use
Verify all settings against network policy and device behaviour
Update network documentation to reflect the changes

steps: 1. Compare the topology in the first image with each port dialog to see which device hangs off each port, since a port should carry only the VLAN that device belongs to.
2. On Switch 1 ports 1–7, strip out VLANs that do not belong to the attached device and leave the correct VLAN active, tagged only where the link is a trunk to another switch.
3. On Switch 1 port 8, match the VLAN list to the attached device (printers use VLAN 60) and remove or untag everything else.
4. On Switch 3 ports 2–8, keep only the VLAN matching the connected client—VLAN 150 for wireless/mobile users, for example—and disable the rest so devices cannot reach other networks.
5. Enable LACP on the ports that form the multiple links between switches and leave duplex on Auto so the aggregated link is redundant and free of duplex mismatch.
6. Finally, disable any port with nothing plugged into it, then verify the running configuration and record the changes.

An access switch should hand each attached device exactly one network. That means the VLAN list on every access port has to mirror what is plugged into it – the server ports carry the server VLAN 90 untagged, the printer port carries VLAN 60, and the mobile-user/WLAN port carries VLAN 150 – while every VLAN that has nothing to do with that device is removed so a host cannot hop onto another subnet. Only the uplinks between switches need multiple tagged VLANs, and those uplinks are the ones that must run LACP so the pair of cables forms a single fault-tolerant aggregated link; leaving duplex on Auto keeps the two ends from mismatching and causing collisions and slow throughput. Anything left over – ports with no device attached – is shut down so an intruder cannot simply plug in and gain access. Once the edits are saved, the settings should be verified against the intended design and the documentation updated so future troubleshooting
reflects the new switch.

prompt: A network technician was recently onboarded to a company. A manager has tasked the technician with documenting the network and has provided the technician with partial information from previous documentation.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on each switch to perform a network discovery by entering commands into the terminal. Type help to view a list of available commands.
Fill in the missing information using the drop-down menus provided.
summary: Use switch discovery commands (show mac-address-table, show vlan, show ip interface brief) to learn each PC's MAC address, IP address, VLAN and switch interface, then fill in the missing values in the drop-down menus.
steps: 1. Click each switch and run a discovery command such as show mac-address-table so that every learned MAC address is tied to a specific access-switch port.
2. Match the MAC addresses learned on Access Switch 1 to PC1 and PC2, and those learned on Access Switch 2 to PC3 and PC4, since the topology fixes which PC hangs off which switch.

3. Use show ip interface brief / the ARP or DHCP data to pair each discovered MAC with its host address; the already-filled fields (PC1 MAC 0200.0000.0003, PC2 IP 10.10.30.51, PC4 IP 10.10.30.53) anchor the remaining choices, and the published answer documents 10.10.30.51 as the address in the PC1 IP column.
4. Run show vlan to see which access ports are in VLAN 10 and which are in VLAN 20, then select that VLAN for the PC sitting on the corresponding port.
5. Read the port name from the MAC address table output (GigabitEthernet0/1 through 0/4) and select the interface that matches the physical cabling shown in the diagram.
6. Verify the finished documentation with show vlan and show running-config so the recorded VLANs and interfaces agree with the live configuration.

This simulation is answered from the switches' own tables rather than from guesswork. The MAC address table on each access switch lists every learned MAC together with the port it was learned on, so it simultaneously tells you which PC owns which MAC and which GigabitEthernet interface that PC is plugged into. Show vlan then reveals the VLAN membership of those same access ports, giving the VLAN value for each PC, and the addressing information (ARP/interface output) links each MAC to its IP address. Because the diagram already fixes PC1 and PC2 to Access Switch 1 and PC3 and PC4 to Access Switch 2, and because several cells are pre-populated (PC1's MAC 0200.0000.0003, PC2's 10.10.30.51, PC4's 10.10.30.53, and PC3 marked as previously inventoried), the discovery output only has to be reconciled with those anchors. The published answer walks through exactly that workflow and records 10.10.30.51 in the PC1 IP address field, then finishes with show vlan and show running-config as verification that the documented VLANs and interfaces match the running network.

prompt: Users are unable to access files on their department share located on file server 2. The network administrator has been tasked with validating routing between networks hosting workstation A and file server 2.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on each router to review output, identify any issues, and configure the appropriate solution.
summary: Inspect the routing tables of Routers A, B and C, mark which router is missing routing information, and install the static route that lets Workstation A reach File Server 2.

pairs.item: Router A - Was a problem found?
Router B - Was a problem found?
Router C - Was a problem found?

steps: 1. Identify the two endpoints from the topology: Workstation A sits in 10.0.1.0/24 behind Router B, while File Server 2 sits in 10.0.5.0/24 behind Router A's Gi1 link to Switch A-2.
2. Check Router B: it has 10.0.0.0/22 connected on Gi3 (which contains Workstation A's 10.0.1.0/24) plus a default route out Gi1 toward Router C, so traffic toward Site A leaves
correctly and no change is needed.
3. Check Router C: it already has static routes 10.0.0.0/22 via Gi1 (toward Router B) and 10.0.4.0/22 via Gi2 (toward Router A), so it can forward the File Server 2 traffic and no change is needed.

4. Check Router A: its table lists only 10.0.6.0/24 and the summarized 10.0.4.0/22 on Gi2 and a default out Gi3, with nothing pointing at the 10.0.5.0/24 segment reached through Gi1, so this is the router with the missing routing information.
5. Mark 'Yes' on Router A and install a static route for destination prefix 10.0.5.0 with mask 255.255.255.0 out interface Gi1, then save and retest access from Workstation A to File Server 2.

The failure is one-directional routing loss, not a client or switch problem: Workstation A's packets are delivered all the way to Router A, but Router A has no entry that points to the 10.0.5.0/24 network where File Server 2 lives. Router A only knows 10.0.6.0/24 and a 10.0.4.0/22 summary on Gi2, and its default route sends anything unknown back out Gi3 toward Router C, so the department share traffic is bounced away from the Switch A-2 segment on Gi1. Routers B and C already have the routes they need (Router B's connected 10.0.0.0/22 plus a default toward Router C, and Router C's statics for both 10.0.0.0/22 and 10.0.4.0/22), which is why both are answered 'No'. Adding the static route 10.0.5.0 255.255.255.0 out Gi1 on Router A gives the last hop a specific, more precise path than its default route, completing the round trip between Workstation A and File Server 2.

prompt: A network administrator has been tasked with configuring a network for a new corporate office. The office consists of two buildings, separated by 50 feet with no physical connectivity. The configuration must meet the following requirements:
Devices in both buildings should be able to access the Internet.
Security insists that all Internet traffic be inspected before entering the network.
Desktops should not see traffic destined for other devices.
INSTRUCTIONS
Select the appropriate network device for each location. If applicable, click on the magnifying glass next to any device which may require configuration updates and make any necessary changes.
Not all devices will be used, but all locations should be filled.
summary: Place the correct network device into each empty (question-mark) location so both buildings reach the Internet, all Internet traffic is inspected, and desktops do not see each

pairs.item: Placeholder below firewall (edge into Building A)
Placeholder inside Building A with desktops
Placeholder between Building A and Building B

steps: 1. Because security requires every Internet-bound packet to be examined, the device that sits directly between the Internet cloud and the rest of the network must be a firewall.
2. Behind the firewall a router is needed to move traffic between the internal networks of Building A and Building B and out to the Internet.
3. Desktops must not see traffic meant for other hosts, so the LAN device in Building A must be a switch rather than a hub, since a switch forwards frames only to the destination port.
4. The two buildings are 50 feet apart with no cabling, so a wireless range extender bridges the gap and carries the wireless signal from Building A to Building B.
5. Inside Building B a switch provides local connectivity for the laptops and mobile devices so they can reach Building A resources and the Internet.

The design works from the outside in. Internet traffic first hits the firewall, which satisfies the security requirement that all inbound and outbound traffic be inspected. The router behind it performs the Layer 3 forwarding that lets both buildings' subnets reach each other and the Internet. Inside Building A the desktops attach to a switch, which keeps unicast frames confined to the destination port so no desktop sees traffic intended for another device (a hub would flood everything and fail this requirement). Since the buildings are separated by 50 feet with no physical cabling, a wireless range extender carries the signal across to Building B, where a second switch gives the local laptops and devices wired connectivity to the rest of the network and out to the Internet.

prompt: A network technician needs to resolve some issues with a customer's SOHO network. The customer reports that some of the devices are not connecting to the network, while others appear to work as intended.
INSTRUCTIONS
Troubleshoot all the network components and review the cable test results by clicking on each device and cable. Type help in each terminal to view a list of available commands.
Diagnose the appropriate component(s) by identifying any components with a problem and recommend a solution to correct each problem.
summary: Inspect the topology, cable test results, VLAN table and printer config, then identify each faulty component and state the remediation for it.
between different VLANs and external networks.

pairs.item: Remediation item 1 - Router and Firewall Configuration
pairs.match: Ensure that all routers are configured with correct static routes to facilitate proper network traffic routing
Install a firewall at the network's entry point to inspect and filter Internet traffic as required by the security policy.
Configure switches to ensure PCs in different VLANs do not see each other's traffic. Implement VLAN tagging on the switches to segregate traffic between the different departments as indicated.
Address any faulty cables as indicated by the test results. For example, any cable showing physical connection issues (crossed pairs, etc.) should be replaced.
Ensure that cables are appropriately labeled and meet the length requirements to avoid potential transmission issues over long distances.

For devices showing incorrect configuration details such as bad IP addresses, subnet masks, or DNS configurations, apply appropriate corrections. For instance, resetting IP configurations or updating DNS settings where mismatches are found.
Check the printer configuration to ensure it aligns with the network settings, particularly the IP address, subnet, and gateway to guarantee connectivity for all users needing access.

Continuously monitor the network for any emerging issues, perform regular updates to the firmware of network devices, and ensure compliance with the latest security standards to maintain network integrity and performance.

steps: 1. Compare each host's IP address against the VLAN Usage table: PC4 (10.10.3.14) belongs to VLAN 3 Marketing and PC3/PC5 (10.10.2.x) to VLAN 2, while the cable feeding PC3 (Cable 4) is left in VLAN 1, so VLAN tagging on the switches must be corrected so departments stay segregated.
2. Read the wire maps in the Cable Test Results: Cable 5, the Switch1-to-Switch2 uplink, shows crossed pairs, so that physical cabling fault must be fixed by replacing the cable.

3. Check the reported cable lengths: Cable 2 at 103M exceeds the 100 m copper Ethernet limit and Cable 8 at 90M is near it, so cables must be labeled and kept within the length limit to avoid transmission problems.

4. Verify each device's addressing: the printer's configuration page shows 10.10.11.56 rather than the documented 10.10.11.16, so IP, subnet mask, gateway and DNS values must be corrected on the misconfigured devices.
5. Finish by making sure routers carry correct routes between VLANs, a firewall filters traffic at the Internet edge, and the network is monitored and kept patched.

The exam's own worked answer treats this simulation as a full troubleshooting write-up rather than a single dropdown. It groups the findings into the areas you inspect in the exhibit: routing and firewall placement so traffic can pass between the VLANs and out to the Internet safely; switch configuration, because hosts such as PC3, PC4 and PC5 sit in

subnets that map to VLAN 2, 3 and 4 in the VLAN Usage table yet some ports are still tagged VLAN 1, letting departments see each other's traffic; the cable tests, where Cable 5's crossed pairs are a physical fault needing replacement and Cable 2's 103 m run breaks the 100 m copper limit; device-specific addressing errors, where a bad IP, mask, gateway or DNS entry must be corrected; and the printer, whose network configuration page reports 10.10.11.56 instead of the documented 10.10.11.16, so its addressing must be realigned with the network. The final point is the general hygiene expected of the technician: keep monitoring, patch firmware, and stay compliant so the corrected network keeps working.

prompt: After a recent power outage, users are reporting performance issues accessing the application servers. Wireless users are also reporting intermittent Internet issues.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on each tab at the top of the screen.
Select a widget to view information, then use the drop-down menus to answer the associated questions.
summary: Use the Network Health and Device Monitoring widgets to pick, from each drop-down, the WAN uplink best suited to VoIP, the device with connectivity problems, and the workstation IP generating the most traffic.

pairs.item: Which WAN station should be preferred for VoIP traffic?
Which device is experiencing connectivity issues?
Which workstation IP is generating the MOST traffic?

steps: 1. Open the WAN Uplinks widget and compare the two circuits on the metrics that matter to real-time voice rather than raw speed.
2. Note that WAN1 shows 2.51% loss, 24 ms latency and 9.5 ms jitter, while WAN2 shows 0.01% loss, 11 ms latency and 3.9 ms jitter, so WAN 2 is the stable path for VoIP even though it is only 1G.
3. In the Device Status widget, look for the entry whose ping fails: Router A at 206.208.133.10 shows 'Request timed out' with 0Gbit/s traffic, marking it as the device with connectivity issues.
4. In the Top Hosts table, ignore router/infrastructure addresses such as 206.208.133.9 and pick the highest-volume workstation, 10.1.90.53 with 13.45 Mp and 80.93 Gb.

Voice traffic tolerates limited bandwidth but not delay, packet loss or variation in delay. The WAN Uplinks widget shows WAN1 is the fat pipe (10G, 353 MBps up) but it suffers 2.51 percent loss, 24 ms average latency and 9.5 ms jitter, and the WAN Health chart also shows WAN1 had noticeable downtime. WAN2, though only 1G, delivers 0.01 percent loss, 11 ms latency and 3.9 ms jitter with full uptime, which is exactly the consistent, low-jitter behaviour VoIP calls need, so WAN 2 is the preferred uplink and WAN1 is better left for bulk data transfers. On the Device Monitoring tab, the Device Status detail table identifies the failing node directly: Router A (206.208.133.10) returns 'Request timed out' and is passing 0Gbit/s, the single 'Down' device in the donut chart. Finally, of the addresses listed in Top Hosts, the top entry 206.208.133.9 is Router B, an infrastructure device, so the busiest workstation is 10.1.90.53, which pushed 13.45 Mp and 80.93 Gb of traffic.

prompt: Which of the following steps of the troubleshooting methodology would most likely include checking through each level of the OSI model after the problem has been identified?
explanation: Creating a plan of action is the step where the technician systematically determines how to troubleshoot the problem, which includes checking through each OSI layer to isolate

where the issue exists. This occurs after the problem is identified but before implementing solutions. Establishing a theory comes after gathering information, implementing the solution is execution, and verifying functionality is the final step.

why.A: Establishing a theory comes after information gathering, not necessarily involving systematic OSI layer checking.
why.B: Implementation is execution of the solution, not the planning/checking phase.
why.D: Verification occurs after the solution is implemented, not during the diagnostic checking phase.

prompt: While troubleshooting a VoIP handset connection, a technician's laptop is able to successfully connect to network resources using the same port.
The technician needs to identify the port on the switch.
Which of the following should the technician use to determine the switch and port?
explanation: LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) allows devices to discover and identify neighboring network devices and the switch ports they are connected to. This is the standard protocol for determining switch identity and port information without requiring manual configuration or network access.

why.B: IKE (Internet Key Exchange) is related to VPN encryption, not device/port discovery.
why.C: VLAN configuration helps segment networks but doesn't identify which physical switch port a device connects to.
why.D: netstat displays network connections and statistics from the local device, not switch port information.

prompt: A network administrator needs to set up a file server to allow user access. The organization uses DHCP to assign IP addresses.
Which of the following is the best solution for the administrator to set up?

options.text: A separate scope for the file server using a /32 subnet
A reservation for the server based on the MAC address
A static IP address within the DHCP IP range

answerText: A reservation for the server based on the MAC
explanation: address

A DHCP reservation binds a specific MAC address to a fixed IP address, ensuring the file server always receives the same IP while remaining under DHCP management. This provides the reliability needed for a server that must be consistently addressable while maintaining DHCP infrastructure benefits.

why.A: A /32 subnet is a single host and creates unnecessary complexity; reservations are simpler.
why.C: Assigning a static IP within the DHCP range can cause conflicts if DHCP also assigns that address.
why.D: SLAAC (Stateless Address Auto-Configuration) is for IPv6 and doesn't provide the centralized control needed for server management.

prompt: Which of the following technologies are X.509 certificates most commonly associated with?
explanation: X.509 certificates are the standard certificate format used within Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) systems for digital authentication, encryption, and identity verification. PKI is the framework that manages, distributes, and validates X.509 certificates.

why.B: VLAN tagging is for network segmentation, unrelated to certificate technology.
why.C: While LDAP can work with certificates, X.509 is most fundamentally associated with PKI, not LDAP specifically.
why.D: MFA uses various authentication factors but X.509 certificates are not its primary association.

prompt: A network administrator wants to implement an authentication process for temporary access to an organization's network.
Which of the following technologies would facilitate this process?
explanation: A captive portal is specifically designed to provide temporary, guest-level network access by presenting an authentication page that users must complete before accessing the network. This is the standard technology for temporary access scenarios.

why.B: Enterprise authentication is designed for permanent organizational users, not temporary access.
why.C: Ad hoc networks are peer-to-peer connections, not suitable for centralized temporary access control.
why.D: WPA3 is a wireless encryption standard, not an authentication/access control technology for temporary users.

prompt: A user is unable to navigate to a website because the provided URL is not resolving to the correct IP address. Other users are able to navigate to the intended website without issue.
Which of the following is most likely causing this issue?
explanation: A hosts file on the user's local machine can override DNS resolution for specific URLs, causing them to resolve to incorrect IP addresses or not resolve properly while other users are unaffected. This explains why only one user has the issue—it's a local configuration problem rather than a network-wide DNS problem.

why.B: Self-signed certificates cause security warnings, not URL resolution failures.
why.C: Nameserver record issues would affect all users trying to reach the site, not just one user.
why.D: IP helper is used for DHCP relay, not for DNS resolution issues.

prompt: A network administrator is planning to host a company application in the cloud, making the application available for all internal and third-party users.
Which of the following concepts describes this arrangement?
explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) describes a cloud delivery model where a hosted application is made available over the internet for both internal and external users to access. This is the definition of hosting an application in the cloud for organizational and third-party users.

why.A: Multitenancy describes architecture where multiple customers share infrastructure, but doesn't define the service model itself.
why.B: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is infrastructure isolation, not a service delivery model for applications.
why.C: NFV (Network Functions Virtualization) relates to virtualizing network services, not general application hosting.

prompt: Which of the following should be used to obtain remote access to a network appliance that has failed to start up properly?
explanation: Out-of-band management provides remote access to network devices through a separate, independent management channel (such as serial console, IPMI, or dedicated management port) that remains accessible even when the main system has failed. This is essential for recovering devices that won't start normally.

why.A: A crash cart is physical equipment for on-site access, not remote access.
why.B: A jump box is for accessing secured networks, not for direct device recovery during startup failures.
why.C: SSH requires the device to be fully operational, which won't work for a device that failed to start properly.

prompt: Which of the following attacks utilizes a network packet that contains multiple network tags?
explanation: VLAN hopping attacks exploit multiple network tags (double tagging) within a single packet. An attacker inserts an additional 802.1Q tag into a frame, allowing the packet to traverse multiple VLANs and reach restricted network segments. This technique specifically leverages the presence of multiple VLAN tags in a packet structure.

why.A: MAC flooding attacks overwhelm the CAM table with numerous MAC addresses, not involving multiple network tags.
why.C: DNS spoofing involves forging DNS responses to redirect users, unrelated to network packet tagging.
why.D: ARP poisoning uses fraudulent ARP messages to map IP addresses to incorrect MAC addresses, not involving VLAN tags.

prompt: A network administrator is configuring a new switch and wants to connect two ports to the core switch to ensure redundancy.
Which of the following configurations would meet this requirement?
explanation: Link aggregation (also called EtherChannel or bonding) combines multiple physical ports into a single logical link, providing both redundancy and increased bandwidth. When one link fails, traffic automatically flows through the remaining aggregated links, ensuring continuous connectivity to the core switch.

why.A: Full duplex is a communication mode setting, not a redundancy configuration mechanism.
why.B: 802.1Q tagging is a VLAN identification method, not directly related to port redundancy.
why.C: Native VLAN is used for untagged traffic on trunk ports, not for providing redundancy between links.

prompt: Which of the following ports is used for secure email?
explanation: Port 587 is used for SMTP with STARTTLS encryption, providing secure email submission. This port allows clients to authenticate and send email securely through TLS/SSL encryption, making it the standard secure email submission port in modern email infrastructure.

why.A: Port 25 is standard SMTP without encryption, not secure email.
why.B: Port 110 is POP3 without encryption, used for receiving but not secure.
why.C: Port 143 is IMAP without encryption, used for receiving but not secure.

prompt: A client wants to increase overall security after a recent breach.
Which of the following would be best to implement? (Choose two.)
answerText: Least privilege network access; Central policy management
explanation: Least privilege network access (A) restricts users and systems to only the resources they need, reducing breach impact. Central policy management (C) enables consistent security enforcement across all systems and quick remediation when breaches occur. Together, these reduce the attack surface and allow for rapid policy-wide responses to threats.

why.B: Dynamic inventories are useful for asset tracking but don't directly increase security posture after a breach.
why.D: Zero-touch provisioning automates device setup but doesn't address security vulnerabilities from past breaches.
why.E: Configuration drift prevention maintains consistency but is secondary to access controls and policy management.
why.F: Subnet range limits are too granular and don't address the core security improvements needed post-breach.

prompt: Which of the following is a cost-effective advantage of a split-tunnel VPN?

options.text: Web traffic is filtered through a web filler.
More bandwidth is required on the company's internet connection.
Monitoring detects insecure machines on the company's network.
Cloud-based traffic flows outside of the company's network.

answerText: Cloud-based traffic flows outside of the company's
explanation: network.

The cost-effective advantage of split-tunnel VPN is that cloud-based traffic flows outside of the company's network and VPN tunnel, reducing bandwidth consumption on corporate infrastructure. This allows non-sensitive traffic to bypass the VPN while maintaining VPN protection for corporate data, resulting in lower operational costs.

why.A: Web traffic filtering through a web filter is not specific to split-tunnel VPN architecture.
why.B: Split-tunnel reduces bandwidth requirements on the company's connection by routing some traffic directly.
why.C: Monitoring insecure machines is not a cost-effective advantage but rather a security concern of split-tunnel.

prompt: A network technician is troubleshooting a web application's poor performance. The office has two internet links that share the traffic load.
Which of the following tools should the technician use to determine which link is being used for the web application?
explanation: Tracert (traceroute) displays the path packets take through the network to reach a destination, showing each hop and which router/link is used. This allows the technician to determine which of the two internet links is carrying the web application traffic by observing the route taken to reach the web server.

why.A: Netstat shows active connections and network statistics but doesn't reveal which physical link or path is being used.
why.B: Nslookup performs DNS lookups to resolve domain names, unrelated to identifying active data paths.
why.C: Ping tests basic connectivity but doesn't show the path or which specific link is carrying traffic.

prompt: Which of the following attacks can cause users who are attempting to access a company website to be directed to an entirely different website?
explanation: DNS poisoning (also called DNS spoofing) corrupts DNS cache with false DNS records, causing domain names to resolve to attacker-controlled IP addresses. When users attempt to access a company website, the poisoned DNS response redirects them to a completely different website under the attacker's control.

why.B: Denial-of-service attacks make services unavailable but don't redirect users to different websites.
why.C: Social engineering manipulates users through deception but doesn't automatically redirect traffic.
why.D: ARP spoofing redirects traffic to the attacker's machine on the local network, not to an entirely different website.

prompt: As part of an attack, a threat actor purposefully overflows the content-addressable memory (CAM) table on a switch.
Which of the following types of attacks is this scenario an example of?
explanation: MAC flooding attacks intentionally overflow the Content Addressable Memory (CAM) table on a switch by transmitting numerous frames with different source MAC addresses. Once the CAM table is full, the switch cannot learn new MAC addresses and enters fail-open mode, broadcasting frames to all ports, allowing the attacker to sniff network traffic.

why.A: ARP spoofing sends fraudulent ARP replies to redirect traffic, not related to CAM table overflow.
why.B: Evil twin creates a rogue wireless access point, unrelated to CAM table attacks.
why.D: DNS poisoning corrupts DNS records, not involving CAM table manipulation.

prompt: A company's office has publicly accessible meeting rooms equipped with network ports. A recent audit revealed that visitors were able to access the corporate network by plugging personal laptops into open network ports.
Which of the following should the company implement to prevent this in the future?
explanation: Network Access Control (NAC) is specifically designed to authenticate and authorize devices before they can access the network. It prevents unauthorized devices from connecting to network ports by checking device compliance, credentials, and other security policies. This directly addresses the vulnerability where visitors could plug in personal laptops.

why.A: URL filters control web traffic, not physical port access.
why.B: VPN is for remote secure connections, not preventing local port access.
why.C: ACLs control traffic rules but don't prevent unauthorized device connections at the port level.

prompt: A user notifies a network administrator about losing access to a remote file server. The network administrator is able to ping the server and verifies the current firewall rules do not block access to the network fileshare.
Which of the following tools would help identify which ports are open on the remote file server?
explanation: Nmap (Network Mapper) is a specialized tool designed to discover hosts and services on

a network by sending packets and analyzing responses. It identifies which ports are open, closed, or filtered on a target server, making it ideal for determining why the file server is inaccessible by revealing port status.

why.A: Dig queries DNS records, not port status.
why.C: Tracert traces the route packets take but doesn't identify open ports.
why.D: Nslookup performs DNS lookups, not port scanning.

prompt: Which of the following technologies is the best choice to listen for requests and distribute user traffic across web servers?
explanation: A load balancer is specifically designed to listen for incoming client requests and distribute them across multiple backend servers based on various algorithms. It handles traffic distribution, health checks, and session persistence, which are the core functions needed for this scenario.

why.A: Routers direct traffic between networks but don't distribute load across servers.
why.B: Switches connect devices within a network but don't distribute application traffic.
why.C: Firewalls filter traffic but don't distribute requests across multiple servers.

prompt: A company is hosting a secure server that requires all connections to the server to be encrypted. A junior administrator needs to harden the web server. The following ports on the web server are open:
Which of the following ports should be disabled?
explanation: Port 80 is used for unencrypted HTTP traffic, which violates the requirement that all connections must be encrypted. Port 443 (HTTPS) provides encrypted web traffic and should remain open. Port 22 (SSH) is commonly used for secure remote administration. Port 587 (SMTP) is used for encrypted email transmission. Since the company requires all connections to be encrypted, port 80 must be disabled to prevent unencrypted HTTP connections.

why.A: Port 22 (SSH) provides encrypted remote access and should remain enabled for secure administration.
why.C: Port 443 (HTTPS) provides encrypted web connections and is essential for meeting the encryption requirement.
why.D: Port 587 (SMTP TLS) provides encrypted email transmission and should remain enabled for encrypted communications.

prompt: Which of the following is the next step to take after successfully testing a root cause theory?

options.text: Duplicate the problem in a lab.
Implement the solution to the problem.

explanation: The proper troubleshooting methodology after successfully testing and confirming a root cause is to determine the specific resolution steps needed to fix the problem. This comes before implementation and allows for planning the actual fix.

why.B: Duplicating in a lab occurs before testing the theory, not after.
why.C: Presenting for approval happens after determining resolution steps.
why.D: Implementation occurs after determining resolution steps, not immediately after testing the theory.

prompt: A network administrator is configuring a new switch and wants to ensure that only assigned devices can connect to the switch.
Which of the following should the administrator do?
explanation: Port security is a switch feature that limits the number of MAC addresses allowed on a port and can restrict access to only pre-authorized devices. This is the direct mechanism for ensuring only assigned devices can connect to specific switch ports.

why.A: ACLs filter traffic but don't control which devices can physically connect to ports.
why.B: Captive portals are used for guest networks, not device authorization on switch ports.
why.D: Disabling services hardens the switch but doesn't control which devices can connect.

prompt: A customer needs six usable IP addresses.
Which of the following best meets this requirement?
explanation: A /28 subnet mask (255.255.255.240) provides 16 total addresses with 14 usable addresses (16 - 2 for network and broadcast). This is the smallest subnet that meets the requirement of six usable IP addresses while being the most efficient allocation.

why.A: /25 (255.255.255.128) provides 126 usable addresses, more than needed.
why.B: /26 (255.255.255.192) provides 62 usable addresses, more than needed.
why.C: /27 (255.255.255.224) provides 30 usable addresses, more than needed.

prompt: A user reports having intermittent connectivity issues to the company network. The network configuration for the user reveals the following:
•  Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0
•  Default gateway: 192.168.1.254
The network switch shows the following ARP table:
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the user's connection issues?

options.text: A port with incorrect VLAN assigned
A switch with spanning tree conflict
Another PC with manually configured IP
A router with overlapping route tables

answerText: Another PC with manually configured IP
explanation: The user's IP address is 192.168.1.10 on eth4 in VLAN 10. However, looking at the ARP table, we can see that 192.168.1.10 is also assigned to eth6 (0c00.1298.d239) in the

same VLAN 10. This is a classic IP address conflict - two devices on the same network segment have the same IP address configured. This would cause intermittent connectivity as ARP packets would be confused about which MAC address should respond to that IP, leading to inconsistent routing and dropped packets. The user's intermittent connectivity is caused by another PC (or network device) that has manually configured the same IP address (192.168.1.10).

why.A: Both devices with 192.168.1.10 are in VLAN 10, so VLAN assignment is not the issue; the problem is the duplicate IP address itself.
why.B: Spanning tree conflicts would cause all connectivity to fail or brief outages during convergence, not the intermittent issues described here from an IP conflict.
why.D: Overlapping route tables on a router would not cause intermittent connectivity for a single user; this is a local network addressing problem, not a routing problem.

prompt: Which of the following is created to illustrate the effectiveness of wireless networking coverage in a building?
explanation: A heat map is a graphical representation that uses colors (typically from cool to warm) to illustrate data density or intensity across a geographic area. In wireless networking, heat maps display signal strength and coverage effectiveness throughout a building.

why.A: Logical diagrams show network topology and connections, not coverage intensity.
why.B: Layer 3 diagrams illustrate IP addressing and routing, not wireless coverage.
why.C: Service-level agreements are documents defining performance standards, not visual coverage illustrations.

prompt: Which of the following cloud deployment models is most commonly associated with multitenancy and is generally offered by a service provider?
explanation: Public cloud is the deployment model most commonly associated with multitenancy, where multiple organizations share the same infrastructure and resources provided by a third-party service provider. It is the standard offering model for most cloud providers.

why.A: Private cloud is dedicated to a single organization, not multitenant.
why.B: Community cloud serves specific organizations but is not the most common multitenancy model.
why.D: Hybrid cloud combines private and public elements but is not primarily defined by multitenancy.

prompt: A network administrator needs to create an SVI on a Layer 3-capable device to separate voice and data traffic.
Which of the following best explains this use case?

options.text: A physical interface used for trunking logical ports
A physical interface used for management access
A logical interface used for the routing of VLANs
A logical interface used when the number of physical ports is insufficient

answerText: A logical interface used for the routing of VLANs
explanation: A Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) is a logical interface created on a Layer 3 switch to enable routing between VLANs. SVIs allow the separation and routing of traffic from different VLANs (such as voice and data) through a single logical interface, enabling inter-VLAN communication while maintaining traffic separation.

why.A: Physical interfaces are used for trunking; SVIs are logical constructs, not physical.
why.B: While SVIs can be used for management, the primary use case here is VLAN routing, not management access.
why.D: SVIs provide routing capabilities for VLANs, not a workaround for insufficient physical ports.

prompt: A network administrator is performing a refresh of a wireless environment. As the APs are being placed, they overlap a little bit with each other.
Which of the following 2.4GHz channels should be selected to ensure that they do not conflict?
explanation: The 2.4GHz Wi-Fi band has 11 usable channels in most regions, but only channels 1, 6, and 11 are non-overlapping. These channels are spaced 5 channels apart, providing sufficient separation to prevent interference when access points overlap. Using these three channels ensures minimal co-channel and adjacent-channel interference.

why.A: Channels 1, 3, and 5 overlap significantly; channel 3 overlaps with both 1 and 5.
why.C: Channels 2, 6, and 10 have overlap issues; channel 2 overlaps with 1 and 6, and channel 10 may not be available in all regions.
why.D: Channels 3, 6, and 9 have overlapping frequencies that would cause interference between adjacent APs.

prompt: Which of the following network cables involves bouncing light off of protective cladding?
explanation: Multimode fiber uses multiple light paths (modes) that bounce off the protective cladding at different angles as they travel through the core. This characteristic defines multimode fiber and distinguishes it from single-mode fiber, which uses a single light path with minimal bouncing off the cladding.

why.A: Twinaxial is a copper-based cable, not fiber optic.
why.B: Coaxial is a copper-based cable with a center conductor, not fiber optic.
why.C: Single-mode fiber uses a single light path with minimal reflection off the cladding, not bouncing.

prompt: Which of the following would allow a network administrator to analyze attacks coming from the internet without affecting latency?
explanation: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) operates passively in a monitoring mode, analyzing traffic for signs of attacks without actively blocking or modifying traffic. This approach allows threat analysis without introducing latency, as IDS can be deployed out-of-band or in a tap configuration to observe traffic without being inline.

why.A: An IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) actively blocks threats inline, which adds latency to traffic flow.
why.C: A load balancer distributes traffic but is not designed for attack analysis.
why.D: A firewall actively processes and filters traffic, introducing latency as part of its blocking function.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting wireless connectivity near a break room. Whenever a user turns on the microwave, connectivity to the user's laptop is lost.
Which of the following frequency bands is the laptop most likely using?
explanation: Microwave ovens operate at 2.4GHz, the same frequency band used by Wi-Fi and many other wireless devices. The electromagnetic radiation from microwaves causes significant
interference in the 2.4GHz band, leading to wireless connectivity loss. The 5GHz, 6GHz, and 900MHz bands are not affected by microwave interference.

why.B: 5GHz Wi-Fi is not significantly affected by microwave oven interference.
why.C: 6GHz is a newer Wi-Fi band that does not overlap with microwave frequencies.
why.D: 900MHz is not a standard Wi-Fi band and is not affected by microwave interference.

prompt: A network administrator needs to implement routing capabilities in a hypervisor.
Which of the following should the administrator most likely implement?
explanation: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) enables the implementation of network functions, including routing, as software-based virtual functions running on hypervisors rather than dedicated hardware appliances. This allows routing capabilities to be deployed and managed within a virtualized environment.

why.A: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a cloud service offering, not a hypervisor routing capability.
why.B: A firewall is a security function, not a routing implementation within a hypervisor.
why.D: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) is a cloud service model, not a specific routing technology.

prompt: A network technician needs to install patch cords from the UTP patch panel to the access switch for a newly occupied set of offices. The patch panel is not labeled for easy jack identification.
Which of the following tools provides the easiest way to identify the appropriate patch panel port?
explanation: A toner probe (tone generator and tracer) is specifically designed to identify cable runs from a patch panel to their destinations. By sending an audible tone down a cable at the patch panel, the technician can use the probe to detect which port the cable connects to at the switch, making it the most efficient tool for identifying unlabeled ports.

why.B: A laptop can test connectivity but requires the cable to be properly connected and patched, which is what the technician is trying to accomplish.
why.C: A cable tester verifies cable integrity but does not identify which physical port a cable connects to.
why.D: A visual fault locator detects breaks in fiber optic cables and is not applicable to identifying patch panel ports.

prompt: A network administrator received complaints of intermittent network connectivity issues. The administrator investigates and finds that the network design contains potential loop scenarios.
Which of the following should the administrator do?
explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is designed specifically to detect and prevent network loops by blocking redundant paths while maintaining backup connections. Enabling spanning tree on switches in a topology with loop scenarios will eliminate the loops causing intermittent connectivity issues while preserving network redundancy.

why.B: Port security restricts access based on MAC addresses but does not prevent switching loops.
why.C: Changing switch port speeds does not address the root cause of loops or prevent broadcast storms.
why.D: 802.1Q tagging is for VLAN configuration and does not prevent or resolve network loops.

prompt: Which of the following routing technologies uses a successor and a feasible successor?
explanation: EIGRP (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol) is the only routing protocol among the options that uses the concept of a successor (the primary next-hop route with the lowest cost) and a feasible successor (a backup route that meets the feasibility condition). This dual concept is central to EIGRP's fast convergence and loop-free topology guarantees.

why.A: IS-IS uses a shortest path tree but does not employ successor/feasible successor concepts.
why.B: OSPF uses designated routers and shortest path first calculations, not successors and feasible successors.
why.C: BGP uses path vectors and AS-path attributes, not the successor/feasible successor model.

prompt: Which of the following best describes what an organization would use port address translation for?

options.text: Public address on the perimeter router
Non-routable address on the perimeter router

answerText: Non-routable address on the perimeter router
explanation: Port Address Translation (PAT) is used to translate non-routable (private) addresses on internal networks to routable addresses for internet communication. Option C correctly identifies that PAT operates on non-routable addresses on the perimeter router, allowing private internal addresses to communicate externally through address translation.

why.A: VLANs on the perimeter are a network segmentation concept unrelated to PAT functionality.
why.B: Public addresses on the perimeter are already routable and do not require translation via PAT.
why.D: Server placement on the perimeter is a network topology decision separate from the purpose of PAT.

prompt: A company is implementing a wireless solution in a high-density environment.
Which of the following 802.11 standards is used when a company is concerned about device saturation and coverage?
explanation: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) is specifically designed to handle high-density environments with improved device saturation capabilities through features like OFDMA, spatial reuse, and BSS coloring. It provides better performance and coverage in congested areas compared to earlier standards.

why.A: 802.11ac (5 GHz, up to 3.5 Gbps) is older and lacks the high-density optimization features of 802.11ax.
why.C: 802.11g (2.4 GHz, 54 Mbps) is an older standard with limited throughput and poor high-density performance.
why.D: 802.11n predates 802.11ax and does not have the advanced features designed for high-density device saturation scenarios.

prompt: Which of the following network traffic types is sent to all nodes on the network?
explanation: Broadcast traffic is specifically designed to be sent to all nodes on a network segment or subnet. A broadcast address (such as 255.255.255.255 in IPv4) ensures delivery to every host on the local network, making it the defining characteristic of broadcast transmission.

why.A: Unicast sends data to a single specific destination node.
why.C: Multicast sends data to a group of selected nodes that have subscribed to a multicast address.
why.D: Anycast sends data to the nearest node in a group based on routing metrics, not all nodes.

prompt: Which of the following cable types provides the highest possible transmission speed?
explanation: Fiber-optic cable provides the highest transmission speeds among the options, capable of supporting speeds in the terabits per second range. It uses light propagation rather than electrical signals, eliminating electromagnetic interference and allowing for vastly greater bandwidth compared to copper-based alternatives.

why.A: Plenum is a fire-rated cable type classification; it does not determine speed independently.
why.B: Ethernet refers to the protocol/standard, not a specific cable type; speeds vary based on the actual medium used.
why.D: DAC (Direct Attach Copper) is limited to shorter distances and lower speeds compared to fiber-optic technology.

prompt: Which of the following layers of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end encryption?
explanation: The Presentation Layer (Layer 6) is responsible for data encryption, decryption, and formatting. While end-to-end encryption concepts may involve multiple layers, the OSI model designates Layer 6 (Presentation) as the layer responsible for encryption/decryption operations and data translation.

why.B: The Application Layer provides user services and interfaces but delegates encryption responsibilities to lower layers.
why.C: The Session Layer manages sessions and dialog control, not encryption.
why.D: While the Transport Layer can participate in encryption (e.g., TLS), the Presentation Layer is the designated OSI layer for encryption.

prompt: A network security administrator needs to monitor the contents of data sent between a secure network and the rest of the company.
Which of the following monitoring methods will accomplish this task?
explanation: Port mirroring (SPAN - Switched Port Analyzer) copies traffic from a source port to a destination port, allowing a monitoring device to capture and inspect the actual contents of data packets. This is the only method listed that directly captures full packet contents for deep inspection.

why.B: Flow data provides summary statistics about traffic patterns, not detailed packet contents.
why.C: Syslog entries record system events and messages, not the actual contents of data packets.
why.D: SNMP traps are alerts and notifications about network events, not mechanisms for inspecting data contents.

prompt: Which of the following does a full-tunnel VPN provide?

options.text: The ability to reset local computer passwords
Corporate inspection of all network traffic

answerText: Corporate inspection of all network traffic
explanation: A full-tunnel VPN routes all network traffic through the VPN connection to the corporate network, enabling the organization to inspect and monitor all user traffic for security and compliance purposes. This provides complete visibility and control over employee network activity regardless of the destination.

why.A: Full-tunnel VPNs typically increase bandwidth requirements by routing all traffic through the tunnel.
why.B: VPNs do not provide the capability to reset local computer passwords; that requires separate authentication mechanisms.
why.D: Preventing access to blocked sites is the purpose of corporate filtering, and full-tunnel VPNs enforce this but don't inherently enable access to blocked sites.

prompt: Which of the following does a hash provide?
explanation: A hash function provides integrity by generating a unique fingerprint of data that changes if the data is modified. When data is hashed and later rehashed, matching hash values confirm the data has not been altered. Hashes do not provide non-repudiation (which requires digital signatures), confidentiality (hashes are one-way but not encryption), or availability (which is a system characteristic).

why.A: Non-repudiation requires digital signatures, not hashes alone.
why.C: Confidentiality requires encryption; hashes do not encrypt data.
why.D: Availability is a system design concern, not a hash function property.

prompt: A company wants to implement a disaster recovery site for non-critical applications, which can tolerate a short period of downtime.
Which of the following types of sites should the company implement to achieve this goal?
explanation: A warm site is ideal for non-critical applications that can tolerate short downtime. It maintains some systems and data in a ready state but is not fully operational, making it more cost-effective than a hot site while providing faster recovery than a cold site. Hot sites are too expensive for non-critical applications, cold sites have unacceptable recovery times, and passive is not a standard DR site classification.

why.A: Hot sites are fully operational and expensive, unnecessary for non-critical applications.
why.B: Cold sites have long recovery times unsuitable for applications needing minimal downtime.
why.D: Passive is not a recognized disaster recovery site type in standard classifications.

prompt: Which of the following is an XML-based security concept that works by passing sensitive information about users, such as log-in information and attributes, to providers?
explanation: SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based standard that enables single sign-on by securely passing authentication and user attribute information between identity providers and service providers. IAM is a broad concept not XML-based, MFA is
multi-factor authentication unrelated to XML protocols, and RADIUS is an authentication protocol that predates and differs from SAML's XML approach.

why.A: IAM is a management framework, not an XML-based protocol for passing user information.
why.B: MFA is multi-factor authentication, not an XML-based federation standard.
why.C: RADIUS is a protocol for authentication but uses a different mechanism, not XML.

prompt: Which of the following routing technologies uses unequal cost load balancing and port 88?
explanation: EIGRP (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol) supports unequal cost load balancing through its variance parameter and uses port 88 for communication between routers. BGP uses port 179, OSPF uses IP protocol 89 (not a port), and RIP does not support unequal cost load balancing.

why.B: BGP uses port 179, not port 88.
why.C: RIP does not support unequal cost load balancing.
why.D: OSPF uses IP protocol 89 and does not support unequal cost load balancing.

prompt: A wireless network consultant is deploying a large number of WAPs and wants to centrally control them from one wireless LAN controller.
Which of the following network types should the consultant employ?
explanation: An infrastructure network topology is the standard enterprise wireless architecture where multiple WAPs (wireless access points) are centrally managed by a wireless LAN controller. This allows centralized configuration, security policies, and roaming. Mesh networks are self-healing but decentralized, point-to-point links two devices, and ad hoc networks operate without central control.

why.A: Mesh networks are decentralized and self-healing, not controlled by a central controller.
why.C: Point-to-point connects only two devices, not suitable for multiple WAPs.
why.D: Ad hoc networks lack centralized control and are not designed for enterprise deployment.

prompt: Which of the following network topologies involves sending all traffic through a single point?
explanation: A hub-and-spoke topology routes all traffic through a central hub or core point, making it a centralized architecture. This is contrasted with mesh topologies where devices connect directly, hybrid topologies that combine multiple approaches, and point-to-point which connects only two devices directly.

why.A: Mesh topology allows direct device-to-device connections without a single central point.
why.B: Hybrid topology combines multiple topologies but does not necessarily route all traffic through one point.
why.D: Point-to-point topology directly connects two devices without a central hub.

prompt: Which of the following functions is used to prioritize network traffic based on the type of traffic?
explanation: QoS (Quality of Service) is the function that prioritizes network traffic based on traffic type, application, or other criteria to ensure optimal performance for critical applications. VPN provides encryption and tunneling, CDN distributes content geographically, and TTL controls packet lifetime in the network.

why.B: VPN provides secure tunneling and encryption, not traffic prioritization.
why.C: CDN distributes content across multiple locations, not for traffic prioritization.
why.D: TTL limits packet lifespan to prevent infinite loops, not for traffic prioritization.

prompt: Which of the following most likely determines the size of a rack for installation? (Choose two.)
explanation: Switch depth and server height are the primary physical factors determining rack size. The depth of network switches and the height of servers (measured in rack units) directly determine the minimum rack dimensions needed to accommodate equipment. KVM size, hard drive size, cooling fan speed, and outlet amperage affect operational considerations but not the fundamental physical rack size.

why.A: KVM size is a minor peripheral consideration and does not determine rack dimensions.
why.C: Hard drive size is an internal component and does not impact rack physical dimensions.
why.D: Cooling fan speed is a performance specification that does not determine rack size.
why.E: Outlet amperage is an electrical specification relevant to power but not physical rack sizing.

prompt: A network administrator is planning to implement device monitoring to enhance network visibility. The security team requires that the solution provides authentication and encryption.
Which of the following meets these requirements?
explanation: SNMPv3 is the only option that provides both authentication and encryption for device monitoring. SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c lack security features, while SNMPv3 includes authentication (using MD5 or SHA) and encryption (using DES or AES) capabilities. SIEM, Syslog, and NetFlow do not inherently provide authentication and encryption at the protocol level for monitoring itself.

why.A: SIEM is a log management and analysis tool, not a protocol that provides authentication and encryption for device monitoring.
why.B: Syslog transmits logs in plaintext without authentication or encryption.
why.C: NetFlow collects traffic flow data but does not provide authentication or encryption mechanisms.

prompt: A network administrator needs to change where the outside DNS records are hosted.
Which of the following records should the administrator change at the registrar to accomplish this task?
explanation: NS (Name Server) records are what must be changed at the registrar to point to a new DNS hosting provider. NS records tell the DNS system which servers are authoritative for a domain. Changing these at the registrar delegates DNS authority to the new hosting provider's servers.

why.B: SOA records are managed at the DNS server level, not at the registrar.
why.C: PTR records are used for reverse DNS lookups and are not changed at the registrar.
why.D: CNAME records are DNS records that create aliases and are not used to change DNS hosting providers.

prompt: A support agent receives a report that a remote user's wired devices are constantly disconnecting and have slow speeds. Upon inspection, the support agent sees that the user's coaxial modem has a signal power of -97dB.
Which of the following should the support agent recommend to troubleshoot the issue?

options.text: Removing any splitters connected to the line
Moving the devices closer to the modem

answerText: Removing any splitters connected to the line
explanation: A signal power of -97dB is extremely weak (normal is typically -10 to -7dB for downstream). Splitters cause signal loss and attenuation; removing them will improve signal strength and resolve disconnections and slow speeds. This is a physical layer issue that requires improving the signal quality at the modem.

why.B: Switching to wireless would not address the underlying modem signal issue and would not resolve wired device problems.
why.C: Moving devices closer to the modem does not address weak incoming signal from the ISP line.
why.D: Lowering network speed does not address the root cause of weak signal power affecting connection stability.

prompt: Which of the following does OSPF use to communicate routing updates?
explanation: OSPF uses multicast addresses (224.0.0.5 for OSPF routers and 224.0.0.6 for designated routers) to communicate routing updates. Multicast allows OSPF to efficiently send updates to only relevant routers rather than broadcasting to all devices on the network.

why.A: OSPF does not use unicast for standard routing updates; it uses multicast for efficiency.
why.B: Anycast is not used by OSPF for routing updates.
why.D: Broadcast would reach all devices on a segment, which is inefficient; OSPF uses targeted multicast instead.

prompt: A storage network requires reduced overhead and increased efficiency for the amount of data being sent.
Which of the following should an engineer most likely configure to meet these requirements?
explanation: Jumbo frames increase the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size from the standard 1500 bytes to typically 9000 bytes, reducing protocol overhead and increasing efficiency by allowing more data per frame. This directly reduces overhead and increases throughput for storage networks handling large data transfers.

why.A: Link speed determines bandwidth capacity but does not reduce overhead or improve frame efficiency.
why.C: QoS manages traffic prioritization and quality but does not reduce overhead for increased efficiency.
why.D: 802.1q tagging adds VLAN information but increases frame size and overhead rather than reducing it.

prompt: A security administrator is creating a new firewall object for a device with IP address 192.168.100.1/25. However, the firewall software only uses dotted decimal notation in configuration fields.
Which of the following is the correct subnet mask to use?
explanation: A /25 CIDR notation means 25 bits for the network portion and 7 bits for hosts. The subnet mask is calculated as 255.255.255.128 (the first 25 bits set to 1: 11111111.11111111.11111111.10000000 in binary equals 255.255.255.128 in decimal).

why.A: 255.255.254.0 represents a /23 network, not /25.
why.B: 255.255.255.1 is not a valid subnet mask.
why.D: 255.255.255.192 represents a /26 network, not /25.

prompt: Which of the following disaster recovery metrics describes the average length of time a piece of equipment can be expected to operate normally?
explanation: MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) is the average length of time a piece of equipment can be expected to operate normally before a failure occurs. It measures equipment reliability and uptime expectations.

why.A: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.
why.B: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) is the maximum acceptable downtime to restore a system.
why.C: MTTR (Mean Time To Repair) is the average time required to repair a failed component, not how long it operates normally.

prompt: A network administrator logs on to a router and sees an interface with an IP address of 10.61.52.34 255.255.255.252.
Which of the following best describes how this interface IP address is being used?

options.text: As a virtual address for redundancy

explanation: A /30 subnet mask (255.255.255.252) provides only 4 IP addresses total (2 usable for hosts), which is the standard configuration for point-to-point connections between routers. This subnet size is deliberately chosen for serial links and router-to-router connections where only two devices need to communicate.

why.B: Internet connections typically use larger subnets or single IP addresses, not /30 point-to-point networks.
why.C: Virtual addresses for redundancy (HSRP, VRRP) would not be limited to a /30 subnet.
why.D: Out-of-band management typically uses separate management networks, not standard routing interface configurations.

prompt: A network technician is troubleshooting a faulty NIC and tests the theory.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: The CompTIA troubleshooting methodology follows a specific order: identify the problem, establish a theory of probable cause, test the theory, establish a plan of action, implement the solution, verify full system functionality, and document findings. Since the technician has already tested the theory, the next step is to establish a plan of action before implementing any solution.

why.A: Developing a theory comes before testing the theory, which has already been done.
why.C: Implementation comes after establishing a plan of action.
why.D: Documentation is the final step after the solution is implemented and verified.

prompt: A network administrator is configuring access points for installation in a dense environment where coverage is often overlapping.
Which of the following channel widths should the administrator choose to help minimize interference in the 2.4GHz spectrum?
explanation: In the 2.4GHz spectrum, using 20MHz channel width minimizes interference in dense, overlapping coverage environments. The 2.4GHz band has only three non-overlapping channels, and narrower channel widths reduce the likelihood of interference with neighboring access points. Wider channels (40MHz, 80MHz, 160MHz) consume more spectrum and increase interference risk.

why.A: 11MHz is not a standard channel width option for WiFi.
why.C: 40MHz channel width uses twice the spectrum and increases interference in dense deployments.
why.D: 80MHz is not typically available in 2.4GHz and would cause significant interference.
why.E: 160MHz is not available in 2.4GHz spectrum.

prompt: A network manager wants to view network traffic for devices connected to a switch. A network engineer connects an appliance to a free port on the switch and needs to configure the switch port connected to the appliance.
Which of the following is the best option for the engineer to enable?
explanation: Port mirroring (also called SPAN - Switched Port Analyzer) is the correct feature to enable on a switch port. It copies traffic from one or more ports to another port where a monitoring appliance is connected, allowing the administrator to analyze network traffic without disrupting normal operations.

why.A: Trunking is used to carry multiple VLANs across a single link, not for traffic monitoring.
why.C: Full duplex is a connection mode setting that has no relationship to traffic analysis.
why.D: SNMP is a network management protocol for device monitoring, not for capturing traffic on a specific port.

prompt: A network administrator is in the process of installing 35 PoE security cameras. After the administrator installed and tested the new cables, the administrator installed the cameras. However, a small number of the cameras do not work.
Which of the following is the most likely reason?
explanation: When installing multiple PoE devices like 35 security cameras, exceeding the power budget of the PoE switch is the most likely cause of some cameras not working. Each PoE port supplies limited power, and the total power supplied by the switch is finite. Installing many power-hungry devices can exceed this budget, leaving insufficient power for some
cameras.

why.A: Incorrect wiring standards would have been caught during the cable testing phase.
why.C: Signal attenuation affects data transmission but not power delivery, and would not have passed testing.
why.D: Wrong voltage would cause immediate failure of all cameras using that voltage, not just some.

prompt: A network administrator is troubleshooting an application issue after a firewall change. The administrator has confirmed that the port and protocol are accessible to the user, but the application is still having issues.
Which of the following tools allows the administrator to look at traffic on the application layer of the OSI model?
explanation: tcpdump is a packet capture tool that allows analysis of network traffic at multiple OSI layers, including the application layer. It can capture and display detailed packet contents, including application-layer protocols and payloads, making it ideal for troubleshooting application-specific issues after port and protocol accessibility have been confirmed.

why.A: ifconfig is used to view and configure network interfaces, not to analyze application-layer traffic.
why.C: nslookup is used for DNS queries and operates at the application layer but doesn't capture or analyze arbitrary traffic.
why.D: traceroute is used for routing path analysis and operates at the network layer, not the application layer.

prompt: Which of the following ports should a network administrator enable for encrypted log-in to a network switch?
explanation: Port 22 is SSH (Secure Shell), which provides encrypted remote login to network devices including switches. SSH encrypts both authentication and data transmission, making it the secure standard for administrative access to network equipment.

why.B: Port 23 is Telnet, which transmits credentials and data in plaintext without encryption.
why.C: Port 80 is HTTP, which is unencrypted and used for web browsing, not switch administration.
why.D: Port 123 is NTP (Network Time Protocol), used for time synchronization, not administrative access.

prompt: Which of the following is used to stage copies of a website closer to geographically dispersed users?
explanation: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is designed to cache and serve website content from geographically distributed servers located closer to end users. This reduces latency and improves performance by serving content from nearby edge locations rather than a single origin server.

why.A: A VPN creates encrypted tunnels for secure remote access, not for content distribution.
why.C: A SAN (Storage Area Network) is for centralized storage management, not for distributing website content to users.
why.D: SDN (Software-Defined Networking) is an architecture approach for network management, not for content delivery.

prompt: Which of the following appliances provides users with an extended footprint that allows connections from multiple devices within a designated WLAN?
explanation: An access point (AP) is specifically designed to extend wireless network coverage and allow multiple devices to connect to the same WLAN within its designated service area. Access points broadcast SSID beacons and handle wireless client associations to provide extended footprint coverage.

why.A: A router primarily routes traffic between networks and may have limited wireless range compared to dedicated APs.
why.B: A switch operates at layer 2 and provides wired connectivity, not wireless WLAN extension.
why.D: A firewall is a security device that filters traffic, not a device for extending WLAN coverage.

prompt: An administrator is configuring a switch that will be placed in an area of the office that is accessible to customers.
Which of the following is the best way for the administrator to mitigate unknown devices from connecting to the network?
explanation: 802.1X is a port-based network access control (NAC) protocol that requires authentication before devices can connect to the network. It is the best mitigation for preventing unknown devices from connecting, especially in publicly accessible areas, as it validates device credentials before granting network access. This is superior to ACLs alone because it operates at the authentication layer rather than just filtering traffic.

why.A: SSE (Secure Service Edge) is a cloud security architecture, not a device-level network access control mechanism.
why.B: ACLs filter traffic but don't prevent unauthenticated devices from initially connecting to the network.
why.C: A perimeter network is a network design concept that doesn't directly prevent unknown devices from connecting to a local switch.

prompt: Which of the following diagrams would most likely include specifications about fiber connector types?
explanation: A physical diagram shows the actual hardware layout and physical connectivity of network components, including specific details about connector types, cable specifications, and hardware interfaces. Fiber connector types (LC, SC, ST, etc.) are physical specifications that would be included in physical documentation.

why.A: Logical diagrams show IP addresses, routing relationships, and services, not physical connector specifications.
why.C: Rack diagrams show equipment placement within racks but typically don't detail connector types.
why.D: Routing diagrams focus on traffic paths and routing protocol relationships, not physical connector specifications.

prompt: Which of the following is the most likely reason an insurance brokerage would enforce VPN usage?

options.text: To encrypt sensitive data in transit
To comply with data retention requirements

answerText: To encrypt sensitive data in transit
explanation: An insurance brokerage handles highly sensitive financial and personal client information. The primary reason to enforce VPN usage is to encrypt sensitive data in transit, protecting confidential information from interception. This is especially critical for an organization dealing with client financial and healthcare data that requires confidentiality.

why.B: While VPNs can contribute to endpoint security, endpoint protection is typically handled by dedicated security tools, not VPNs alone.
why.C: VPN enforcement alone doesn't directly maintain contractual agreements; compliance with agreements requires multiple security measures.
why.D: Data retention requirements are met through backup and archival policies, not through VPN usage.

prompt: An organization moved its DNS servers to new IP addresses. After this move, customers are no longer able to access the organization's website.
Which of the following DNS entries should be updated?
explanation: NS (nameserver) records specify which servers are authoritative for a domain. When DNS servers move to new IP addresses, the NS records must be updated to point to the new nameserver addresses. This ensures that queries are directed to the correct DNS infrastructure, which is why customers cannot access the website—the old NS records are pointing to the old DNS server IPs.

why.A: AAA records are not a standard DNS record type.
why.B: CNAME records point domain aliases to canonical names; they don't need updating when DNS server IPs change.
why.C: MX records specify mail servers, not DNS servers, and are unrelated to website accessibility.

prompt: Which of the following are environmental factors that should be considered when installing equipment in a building? (Choose two.)
explanation: Fire suppression systems and humidity control are both critical environmental factors for equipment installation. Fire suppression prevents equipment damage and data loss, while humidity control prevents condensation and corrosion that damage sensitive electronics. These directly impact equipment lifespan and reliability in the installation environment.

why.B: UPS location is more of a design choice than an environmental factor to consider during installation.
why.D: Power load is an electrical consideration, not an environmental factor.
why.E: Floor construction type affects weight capacity but is not an environmental factor like temperature or humidity.
why.F: Proximity to MDF is a design consideration, not an environmental factor.

prompt: A customer lost the connection to the telephone system. The administration console is configured with multiple network interfaces and is connected to multiple switches. The network administrator troubleshoots and verifies the following:
The support team is able to connect remotely to the administration console.
Rebooting the switch shows solid link and activity lights even on unused ports.
Rebooting the telephone system does not bring the system back online.
The console is able to connect directly to individual modules successfully.
Which of the following is the most likely reason the customer lost the connection?

options.text: The console software needs to be reinstalled.
The cables to the modules need to be replaced.

explanation: The evidence points to a module failure: the console can connect directly to individual modules successfully (ruling out console or cable issues), the switch shows healthy lights (ruling out switch failure), the remote connection to the console works (ruling out network issues), and rebooting the telephone system doesn't resolve the issue. The most likely cause is that a module failed, preventing the overall system from functioning even though components can be reached individually.

why.A: The switch shows solid link and activity lights on all ports after reboot, indicating it is functioning properly.
why.B: Console software issues would affect all connections, but the console can connect remotely and to individual modules.
