prompt: Following a fire in a data center, the cabling was replaced. Soon after an administrator notices network issues.
Which of the following are the most likely causes of the network issues? (Choose two.)

options.text: The switches are not the correct voltage
The HVAC system was not verified as fully functional after the fire
The VLAN database was not deleted before the equipment was brought back online
The RJ45 cables were replaced with unshielded cables
The wrong transceiver type was used for the new termination
The new RJ45 cables are a higher category than the old ones

answerText: The RJ45 cables were replaced with unshielded cables; The wrong transceiver type was used for the new termination
explanation: When cabling is replaced after a fire, the most likely causes of network issues are: (D) Unshielded cables instead of shielded ones can introduce electromagnetic interference and signal degradation, and (E) Using the wrong transceiver type for new terminations causes incompatibility and connection failures. Switches voltage is unlikely to have changed, VLAN databases are not affected by physical cabling replacement, and using higher category cables would actually improve performance, not cause problems.

why.A: Switch voltage would not be affected by cabling replacement
why.B: HVAC system functionality, while important for equipment, does not directly cause network connectivity issues
why.C: VLAN database deletion is not necessary and would not be the cause of network issues after cabling replacement
why.F: Higher category cables are backward compatible and would not cause network problems

prompt: Cloud computing has the capability to meet increased and decreased demands for computing infrastructure for a short period of time.
Which of the following best describes this characteristic?
explanation: Elasticity describes the cloud's ability to dynamically scale computing resources up or down in response to changing demand over short periods of time. This is a fundamental cloud characteristic that allows organizations to provision additional resources when demand increases and release them when demand decreases. Efficiency relates to resource utilization, multitenancy refers to resource sharing among customers, and scalability describes the ability to handle growth—but elasticity specifically captures the rapid, temporary adjustment capability mentioned in the question.

why.A: Efficiency refers to optimal resource utilization, not the ability to meet fluctuating demands
why.C: Multitenancy describes shared infrastructure among customers, not demand responsiveness
why.D: Scalability describes capacity growth but not the temporary, short-term adjustment characteristic

prompt: Which of the following can also provide a security feature when implemented?
explanation: NAT (Network Address Translation) provides a security benefit by hiding internal network IP addresses from external networks, acting as a form of IP address obfuscation and making it harder for attackers to identify and target internal systems. NAT also creates a natural barrier between internal and external networks. BGP is a routing protocol without inherent security features, FHRP (First Hop Redundancy Protocol) provides gateway redundancy, and EIGRP is an interior routing protocol—none provide security features when implemented.

why.B: BGP is a routing protocol that does not provide security features by itself
why.C: FHRP provides high availability and redundancy for gateways, not security features
why.D: EIGRP is an interior routing protocol focused on efficient path selection, not security

prompt: Which of the following best describes the transmission format that occurs at the transport layer over connectionless communication?
explanation: At the transport layer, connectionless communication (UDP) transmits data in units called datagrams. Datagrams are independent, self-contained packets of data that may arrive out of order and are not guaranteed delivery. Segments are used in connection-oriented (TCP) communication, frames operate at Layer 2, and packets are a general term that can
apply to multiple layers.

why.B: Segments are the transmission unit for TCP (connection-oriented), not UDP (connectionless).
why.C: Frames are the transmission unit at the Data Link Layer, not the Transport Layer.
why.D: Packets is a generic term; datagrams is the specific term for connectionless transport layer units.

prompt: Which of the following is most likely to work with an FC connection and offers more scalability?
explanation: A SAN (Storage Area Network) works with Fibre Channel (FC) connections and provides superior scalability compared to other options. FC is specifically designed for high-speed SAN environments, allowing multiple servers to connect to shared storage with high bandwidth and low latency. DAS (Direct Attached Storage) doesn't scale well, SSE is not a storage technology, and NAS typically uses Ethernet rather than FC.

why.A: DAS is directly attached to individual servers and does not offer the scalability of a SAN.
why.C: SSE (Server-Side Encryption) is a security feature, not a storage architecture.
why.D: NAS typically uses Ethernet connections rather than Fibre Channel protocol.

prompt: A company is moving to a hybrid cloud model. As part of this move the mail server will be moved to the cloud. The systems administrator needs to ensure the mail server continues to receive email.
Which of the following types of DNS records should the systems administrator update?
explanation: MX (Mail Exchange) records are specifically used to direct email traffic to mail servers. When a mail server is moved to the cloud, the MX record must be updated to point to the new cloud-based mail server's address or hostname. NS records define nameservers, PTR records are for reverse DNS lookups, and A records point hostnames to IP addresses but are not the primary mechanism for mail routing.

why.A: NS records identify authoritative nameservers; they don't route mail traffic.
why.B: PTR records are used for reverse DNS lookups, not mail routing.
why.D: A records map hostnames to IPs but don't specify mail server preferences like MX records do.

prompt: A network engineer is configuring network ports in a public office. To increase security, the engineer wants the ports to allow network connections only after authentication.
Which of the following security features should the engineer use?
explanation: 802.1X is an IEEE authentication standard that implements port-based network access control. It requires devices to authenticate before gaining access to network ports, using an authenticator (switch), supplicant (client), and authentication server (RADIUS). This is specifically designed for controlling access to network ports in secure environments. Port security limits MAC addresses, MAC filtering is basic and bypassable, and ACLs control traffic but don't enforce authentication.

why.A: Port security limits the number of MAC addresses but does not require authentication.
why.C: MAC filtering blocks based on known addresses but doesn't enforce authentication protocols.
why.D: ACLs control which traffic is allowed but don't enforce authentication before connection.

prompt: A network administrator is expanding a network and wants to ensure no unauthorized redundant links are present.
Which of the following should the administrator use to identify and block redundant links?
explanation: STP (Spanning Tree Protocol) is designed to prevent redundant links and loops in network topologies. It identifies and blocks redundant paths to prevent bridging loops, while maintaining connectivity through a single active path. SDN is a network architecture, LLDP is a discovery protocol, and OSPF is a routing protocol—none of which prevent unauthorized redundant links.

why.A: SDN is a network management approach but does not prevent or block redundant links.
why.C: LLDP discovers and advertises network information but does not block redundant links.
why.D: OSPF is a routing protocol that works with multiple paths; it doesn't block redundancy.

prompt: A network administrator notices uncommon communication between VMs on ephemeral ports on the same subnet. The administrator is concerned about that traffic moving laterally within the network.
Which of the following describes the type of traffic flow the administrator is analyzing?
explanation: East-west traffic refers to lateral communication between systems on the same network or subnet, as opposed to north-south traffic between a client and external services. The

administrator observing uncommon communication between VMs on the same subnet using ephemeral ports is analyzing east-west traffic flow, which is a key concern for detecting lateral movement attacks within a network segment.

why.B: Point-to-point describes a one-to-one connection but not the directional classification of lateral network traffic.
why.C: Horizontal-scaling refers to adding more instances/resources, not a traffic flow classification.
why.D: Hub-and-spoke describes a network topology, not the direction of traffic between systems on the same subnet.

prompt: Which of the following would be violated if an employee accidentally deleted a customer's data?
explanation: Availability ensures that data and systems are accessible and functional when needed. Accidentally deleting customer data violates availability because the data is no longer accessible, even though it wasn't compromised in terms of confidentiality or integrity in the traditional sense. While deletion does affect integrity technically, availability is the primary CIA principle violated when data is lost or made inaccessible.

why.A: Integrity involves preventing unauthorized modification; deletion is more directly an availability issue.
why.B: Confidentiality involves unauthorized access or disclosure; deletion doesn't breach confidentiality.
why.C: Vulnerability is not a CIA principle; the three principles are Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.

prompt: A network engineer is now in charge of all SNMP management in the organization. The engineer must use a SNMP version that does not utilize plaintext data.
Which of the following is the minimum version of SNMP that supports this requirement?
explanation: SNMPv3 is the minimum version that provides encryption and does not transmit data in plaintext. It supports authentication and privacy (encryption) using protocols like AES and DES. SNMPv1 and v2c both use community strings transmitted in plaintext, making them insecure. SNMPv2u was a proposed version that never achieved widespread adoption and also lacked proper encryption.

why.A: SNMPv1 uses plaintext community strings for authentication.
why.B: SNMPv2c also uses plaintext community strings and is not secure.
why.C: SNMPv2u was a proposed version that did not achieve standardization and lacks encryption.

prompt: A company recently acquired a number of sites and no documentation was provided. A network administrator needs to identify and document all of the digital assets in use.
Which of the following is the best method for the administrator to use?
explanation: Network discovery is the most appropriate method for identifying all digital assets across multiple acquired sites without documentation. It uses automated tools to scan the network, identify devices, services, and systems currently in operation. While physical inventory could complement this, network discovery provides the comprehensive automated approach needed to quickly document unknown infrastructure across multiple sites.

why.A: Availability monitoring tracks whether existing known systems are running, not for discovering unknown assets.
why.B: Packet capture analyzes traffic patterns but does not systematically identify and document all digital assets.
why.C: Physical inventory is labor-intensive and time-consuming compared to automated network discovery for large infrastructure.

prompt: A network administrator recently upgraded a wireless infrastructure with new APs. Users are reporting that, when stationary, the wireless connection drops and reconnects after 20 to 30 seconds. While reviewing the logs, the administrator notices that the APs are changing channels.
Which of the following is the most likely reason for the service interruptions?
explanation: Channel interference is the most likely cause when stationary users experience drops and reconnects every 20-30 seconds while APs are actively changing channels. This pattern indicates the APs are detecting interference on their current channels and automatically switching to avoid it, causing service disruptions. The active channel-switching behavior is a key indicator of dynamic interference conditions rather than configuration issues.

why.B: Roaming misconfiguration typically causes issues during movement between APs, not drops while stationary.
why.C: Network congestion would cause slowness or packet loss, not the regular disconnect/reconnect pattern observed.
why.D: Insufficient coverage would result in consistently weak signal, not periodic drops at regular intervals.

prompt: A network administrator needs to set up a multicast network for audio and video broadcasting.
Which of the following networks would be the most appropriate for this application?
explanation: The 224.0.0.0/24 range is the correct answer because it falls within the Class D multicast address space (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255), which is reserved specifically for multicast traffic including audio and video broadcasting. This is the only option that uses an address range designated for multicast purposes.

why.A: 172.16.0.0/24 is a private unicast address range, not suitable for multicast.
why.B: 192.168.0.0/24 is a private unicast address range, not suitable for multicast.
why.D: 240.0.0.0/24 is reserved for experimental use and future use, not designated for multicast.

prompt: A user connects to a corporate VPN via a web browser and is able to use TLS to access the internal financial system to input a time card.
Which of the following best describes how the VPN is being used?
explanation: This describes a clientless VPN because the user accesses the corporate network through a web browser without installing VPN client software. The user connects via TLS (which provides the encryption) through the browser interface to access internal resources. Clientless VPNs allow remote access without requiring dedicated client applications.

why.B: Client-to-site VPNs typically require VPN client software installation on the user device.
why.C: Full tunnel VPNs encrypt all traffic and require dedicated client software, not just web browser access.
why.D: Site-to-site VPNs connect entire networks or sites, not individual users through browsers.

prompt: A network administrator needs to fail over services to an off-site environment. This process will take four weeks to become fully operational.
Which of the following DR concepts does this describe?
explanation: A cold site describes a failover scenario that takes four weeks to become fully operational. Cold sites are pre-configured physical locations with infrastructure but no running systems or current data; they require significant time to restore services. This contrasts with hot sites (immediate failover) and warm sites (hours to days), making cold sites appropriate for non-critical recovery with extended RTO requirements.

why.A: A hot site is immediately available and operational, not requiring four weeks.
why.B: A warm site typically takes hours to days to become operational, not four weeks.
why.D: Active-active approach provides real-time redundancy with simultaneous operation, not a four-week failover process.

prompt: A security analyst wants to control internet access based on site reputation and categorization. The analyst needs a solution that does not require traffic flow changes.
Which of the following solutions would most likely meet these requirements?
explanation: DNS filtering is the best solution for controlling internet access based on site reputation and categorization without requiring traffic flow changes. DNS filtering intercepts DNS queries and blocks or allows access based on domain categorization before the connection is established. It requires no changes to network topology or traffic routing, making it transparent to implement.

why.A: Proxies require traffic flow changes and explicit configuration or client setup to route traffic through them.
why.C: Router ACLs require traffic flow analysis and configuration changes to the network infrastructure.
why.D: Load balancers distribute traffic across servers but do not perform content filtering or site categorization.

prompt: A wireless technician wants to implement a technology that will allow user devices to automatically navigate to the best available frequency standard.
Which of the following technologies should the technician use?
explanation: Band steering is the technology that automatically directs user devices to the best available frequency standard (2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz bands). This feature on APs intelligently navigates dual-band capable devices to the optimal band based on signal strength, congestion, and device capability, improving overall wireless performance.

why.B: A wireless LAN controller manages multiple APs but does not specifically handle automatic band selection for devices.
why.C: A directional antenna focuses signal in specific directions but does not steer devices between frequency bands.
why.D: An autonomous access point operates independently but does not provide intelligent band steering capabilities.

prompt: A user called the help desk after business hours to complain that files on a device are inaccessible and the wallpaper was changed. The network administrator thinks that this issue is an isolated incident, but the security analyst thinks the issue might be a ransomware attack.
Which of the following troubleshooting steps should be taken first?
explanation: Identifying the problem is the first step in the troubleshooting methodology. Before establishing theories, planning actions, or documenting findings, the administrator must gather complete information about the symptoms (inaccessible files and changed wallpaper) and determine if this is truly an isolated incident or part of a larger issue. This information gathering is essential before proceeding to hypothesis and planning.

why.B: Establishing a theory comes after identifying the problem and gathering complete information.
why.C: Documenting findings occurs after investigation and resolution, not at the beginning.
why.D: Creating a plan of action requires identifying the problem first to determine the appropriate response.

prompt: A data center interconnect using a VXLAN was recently implemented. A network engineer observes slow performance and fragmentation on the interconnect.
Which of the following technologies will resolve the issue?
explanation: Jumbo frames increase the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size, allowing larger packets to be transmitted without fragmentation. VXLAN adds a 50-byte header to encapsulated packets, which with standard 1500-byte MTU frames causes fragmentation. Jumbo frames (typically 9000 bytes) accommodate this overhead and resolve both fragmentation and associated performance issues.

why.A: 802.1Q tagging is for VLAN identification and does not address fragmentation in VXLAN overlays.
why.B: Spanning tree prevents loops but does not resolve fragmentation or performance issues.
why.C: Link aggregation increases bandwidth but does not prevent fragmentation caused by oversized VXLAN packets.

prompt: A new server is deployed in a trusted zone and is validated to be online with all appropriate services running. However, users in a perimeter network cannot access the server.
Which of the following should a network administrator do to resolve the reported issue?

options.text: Create a TXT record on the DNS server for the new server.
Update the firewall ACL to allow access to the new server.
Configure a static route for the user VLAN to the new server.
Insert a static ARP entry for the new server on the Layer 3 switch.

answerText: Update the firewall ACL to allow access to the new
explanation: server.

When a new server in a trusted zone is unreachable from a perimeter network, the firewall ACL is the most likely cause. Firewalls enforce security policies between network zones, and without explicit ACL rules allowing traffic from the perimeter to the trusted zone, the connection will be blocked regardless of the server's operational status.

why.A: TXT records are used for verification and do not enable network connectivity.
why.C: Static routes are unnecessary when both zones are already connected through the firewall.
why.D: Static ARP entries are not required for inter-zone communication and do not bypass firewall restrictions.

prompt: Network administrators are using the Telnet protocol to administer network devices that are on the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet.
Which of the following tools should the administrator use to best identify the devices?
explanation: Nmap is a network scanning tool designed to discover active hosts and open ports on a network. It efficiently identifies all devices on the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet and can detect which ones have Telnet (port 23) open for administration, making it ideal for this task.

why.A: Dig is a DNS query tool for hostname-to-IP resolution, not device discovery.
why.C: Tracert traces the path to a single destination and does not discover all devices on a subnet.
why.D: Telnet is a connection protocol, not a discovery tool; it requires knowing the target device already.

prompt: A network administrator recently updated configurations on a Layer 3 switch. Following the updates, users report being unable to reach a specific file server.
Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: A Layer 3 switch configuration update most commonly causes access problems when ACLs are modified. Incorrect ACLs can block traffic to the file server even though the device is reachable. This is the most probable cause following a configuration change, whereas the other options would typically produce different symptoms or wouldn't be caused by a recent update.

why.B: A switching loop causes widespread network issues, not isolated access to one server.
why.C: Duplicate IP addresses would cause intermittent connectivity for the affected device, not complete unreachability.
why.D: Wrong default routes would affect all traffic, not just access to a specific server.

prompt: A network engineer wants to implement a solution where all web servers will send event data over port 514.
Which of the following services will accomplish this task?
explanation: Syslog is the standard protocol for collecting and forwarding system log messages and event data from network devices and servers. It uses UDP port 514 by default, matching the requirement exactly. Syslog allows centralized logging of events from web servers and other network devices.

why.B: SMTP is for email transmission, not event data collection.
why.C: DNS is for hostname resolution, not event logging.
why.D: DHCP is for IP address assignment, not event data transmission.

prompt: A security administrator wants to discover zero-day attacks before they can be used on the company’s network.
Which of the following can the administrator use to accomplish this task?
explanation: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to attract and capture attacks. By deploying honeypots that mimic legitimate services, security administrators can observe and analyze attack techniques before they target production systems, making it the best way to discover and study zero-day exploits.

why.A: A central repository stores data but does not actively detect or attract attacks.
why.C: Next-generation firewalls detect known threats but struggle with zero-day attacks by definition.
why.D: An evil twin is a rogue wireless access point used in attacks, not a detection mechanism.

prompt: Users at a satellite office are experiencing issues when using videoconferencing.
Which of the following should a technician focus on first to rectify these issues?
explanation: Quality of Service (QoS) is the primary focus for videoconferencing issues at a satellite office. QoS prioritizes real-time traffic like video and audio, ensuring adequate bandwidth and low latency. Implementing QoS policies directly addresses the buffering, lag, and dropped calls typical of videoconferencing problems.

why.B: Network signal applies to wireless strength, not overall videoconferencing quality.
why.C: Time to Live (TTL) affects routing but not videoconferencing quality.
why.D: Load balancing distributes traffic but does not prioritize real-time communication flows.

prompt: A network administrator is trying to locate the switch interface a PC is connected to. The administrator accesses the local switch, pings the PC IP address, and then uses the command show arp.
Which of the following commands should the administrator use next?
explanation: After pinging the PC and viewing the ARP table, the next logical step is to use 'show mac-address-table' to identify which switch interface the PC's MAC address is associated with. This command directly maps MAC addresses to physical switch ports, allowing the administrator to locate where the PC is connected.

why.A: Show route displays routing information, not interface associations.
why.C: Show VLAN displays VLAN membership but not specific interface connections.
why.D: Show interface displays port details but requires already knowing the port number.

prompt: A user attempts to log in to a corporate website by utilizing a shortcut. The shortcut has been used many times before. The user then notices some discrepancies on the company website.
Which of the following is most likely the reason for this issue?
explanation: DNS poisoning is the most likely cause because the user is accessing the website through a saved shortcut (which typically contains a domain name), and if DNS has been poisoned, the domain name resolves to a malicious IP address instead of the legitimate corporate server. This would cause the website to appear different while using the same familiar shortcut. The other attacks target different layers: VLAN hopping targets network segmentation, ARP spoofing targets local network traffic, and MAC flooding targets switch operations.

why.A: VLAN hopping would not typically affect a website accessed via shortcut unless the entire network architecture changed.
why.B: ARP spoofing affects local network traffic resolution, not website content accessed via domain names.
why.D: MAC flooding is a denial-of-service attack on switches and would cause connectivity loss, not content discrepancies.

prompt: Which of the following is the correct order of components in a bottom-up approach for the three-tier hierarchical model?
explanation: In the three-tier hierarchical network model using a bottom-up approach, the order is Access (bottom), Distribution (middle), and Core (top). The Access layer connects end devices, the Distribution layer aggregates and filters traffic, and the Core layer provides fast backbone connectivity. This is the standard reference model for enterprise network design.

why.B: Core, root, and distribution is not the standard three-tier model terminology.
why.C: Core, spine, and leaf describes a leaf-spine architecture, which is a different modern topology not the traditional three-tier model.
why.D: Access, core, and root omits the Distribution layer which is essential to the three-tier model.

prompt: A client with a 2.4GHz wireless network has stated that the entire office is experiencing intermittent issues with laptops after the WAP was moved.
Which of the following is the most likely reason for these issues?

options.text: The network uses a non-overlapping channel.
The signal is reflecting too much.
A microwave is in the office.

answerText: A microwave is in the office.
explanation: A microwave oven is the most likely culprit because it operates on the 2.4GHz frequency band and causes significant electromagnetic interference in that range. Since the WAP was recently moved, it may now be positioned closer to a microwave or other 2.4GHz interference source. Microwaves are a well-known cause of intermittent wireless connectivity issues in office environments. While excessive noise could also cause problems, the specific mention of a 2.4GHz network and a recent move makes microwave interference the most direct explanation.

why.A: Non-overlapping channels would actually help prevent interference, not cause it.
why.B: Signal reflection (multipath) typically causes slower performance or dead zones but not the kind of intermittent office-wide issues described.
why.C: While excessive noise is possible, the most common and likely cause in a 2.4GHz office environment is microwave interference specifically.

prompt: Which of the following SD-WAN features allows a router to be shipped directly to the installation site and does not require site-level configuration?
explanation: Zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) is the SD-WAN feature that allows routers to be shipped directly to an installation site and automatically configure themselves without requiring manual site-level configuration. The router automatically connects to a central management platform, downloads its configuration, and becomes operational. This is a key SD-WAN capability that reduces deployment time and complexity.

why.B: Application aware routing is a capability that optimizes traffic based on application types, not an auto-configuration feature.
why.C: Transport agnostic means SD-WAN can work over any connection type, but it doesn't enable automatic provisioning.
why.D: Central policy management is about centralized control of policies, not the automatic configuration of new devices.

prompt: A network technician is troubleshooting network latency and has determined the issue to be occurring between two network switches (Switch10 and Switch11). Symptoms reported include poor video performance and slow file copying. Given the following information:
Which of the following should the technician most likely do to resolve the issue?

options.text: Change the native VLAN on the ports.

explanation: The issue is a mismatch in MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) sizes between the two switches. Switch10 has an MTU of 1600 bytes while Switch11 has an MTU of 1500 bytes. This mismatch causes packet fragmentation and reassembly, leading to increased latency and poor performance for bandwidth-intensive activities like video streaming and file copying. Modifying Switch10's MTU to 1500 bytes to match Switch11 will eliminate this fragmentation issue and resolve the latency problem.

why.A: Automatic negotiation on Switch11 is functioning correctly and is not the cause of the latency issue.
why.C: STP configuration is unnecessary; this is a layer 2 protocol issue unrelated to the MTU mismatch causing latency.
why.D: Native VLAN configuration is not related to the MTU size mismatch that is causing the performance degradation.

prompt: Which of the following types of routes will take precedence when building a routing table for a given subnet?
explanation: Static routes take the highest precedence in a routing table. They are assigned a lower administrative distance (typically 1 or 0) compared to dynamic routing protocols: BGP has an administrative distance of 20 for eBGP and 200 for iBGP, and OSPF has 110. Default routes have the lowest precedence. Administrative distance determines which route source is preferred when multiple routes to the same destination exist.

why.B: BGP has a higher administrative distance (20) than static routes (1), so it has lower precedence.
why.C: OSPF has an administrative distance of 110, making it lower precedence than static routes.
why.D: Default routes are fallback routes with the lowest precedence of all routing sources.

prompt: Which of the following steps in the troubleshooting methodology comes after using a top-to-bottom examination of the OSI model to determine cause?
explanation: After examining the OSI model from top to bottom to determine the cause, the next step in the troubleshooting methodology is to test the theory to confirm the identified cause. The full troubleshooting process is: identify the problem, establish a plan of action, test the theory, verify full system functionality, and document the solution. Testing the theory validates the hypothesis developed from the OSI model examination.

why.B: Establishing a plan of action comes before examining the OSI model, not after.
why.C: Verifying full system functionality is a later step that comes after successfully testing the theory.
why.D: Identifying the problem comes before the top-to-bottom OSI examination, not after.

prompt: Which of the following would an adversary do while conducting an evil twin attack?

options.text: Trick users into using an AP with an SSID that is identical to a legitimate network.
Manipulate address resolution to point devices to a malicious endpoint.
Present an identical MAC to gain unauthorized access to network resources.
Capture data in transit between two legitimate endpoints to steal data.

answerText: Trick users into using an AP with an SSID that is
explanation: identical to a legitimate network.

In an evil twin attack, an adversary creates a rogue wireless access point that broadcasts the same SSID as a legitimate network. Users unknowingly connect to the attacker's AP instead of the real one, allowing the attacker to intercept traffic and credentials. This is the defining characteristic of an evil twin attack.

why.B: Manipulating address resolution describes ARP spoofing or DNS poisoning, not evil twin attacks.
why.C: Presenting an identical MAC describes MAC spoofing, a different type of attack.
why.D: Capturing data between two legitimate endpoints describes packet sniffing or man-in-the-middle attacks, not specifically evil twin attacks.

prompt: An ISP provided a company with an IP range of 98.174.235.142/28. A network technician configured a router with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.224 and default gateway of 98.174.235.129. After the configuration was set up. the company is unable to connect to the ISP.
Which of the following would resolve this issue?

options.text: Change the Ethernet cable from the external interface to the modem.

explanation: The /28 CIDR notation provides 16 total addresses with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.240 (not .224). The technician used subnet mask 255.255.255.224 (which is /27 and provides 32 addresses), making the gateway address 98.174.235.129 invalid for the /28 range. With /28, the valid range in that block is 98.174.235.128-142 with gateway 98.174.235.129, but the wrong subnet mask prevents proper calculation. Changing the subnet mask to .240 (/28) aligns the configuration with the ISP-provided /28 range.

why.B: Changing the Ethernet cable is a physical layer troubleshooting step that wouldn't address the subnet mask mismatch issue.
why.C: Changing to /29 would make the problem worse by further restricting the address space.
why.D: The IP 98.174.235.128/28 is correct, but the real issue is the subnet mask being .224 instead of .240.

prompt: A network administrator is troubleshooting a connection between two switches that is experiencing intermittent errors. The administrator needs to determine which port on the remote switch the faulty cable is connected to.
Which of the following is the best tool to use to identify the error?
explanation: LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) is used to discover and identify neighboring network devices. Running LLDP allows the administrator to see which port on the remote switch the cable is connected to, making it the best tool for identifying the physical connection point of a faulty cable between switches.

why.A: tracert traces the route packets take to a destination, not useful for identifying physical switch ports
why.C: nmap scans for open ports and services on devices, not for discovering physical switch port connections
why.D: ping tests basic connectivity but does not identify which remote switch port a cable is connected to

prompt: Which of the following is a difference between EOL and EOS?

options.text: EOL discontinues the product but may offer support.
EOS replaces free support with a subscription model.
EOS only applies to physical products.

answerText: EOL discontinues the product but may offer support.
explanation: End of Life (EOL) marks when a product is discontinued but may still receive limited support, while End of Support (EOS) means support completely ends. Option A correctly captures that EOL discontinues the product but may offer support, distinguishing it from EOS which provides no support.

why.B: EOS does not necessarily replace free support with a subscription model; it typically means support ends entirely
why.C: Both EOL and EOS apply to both physical and software products
why.D: EOL does not guarantee warranty service; warranties typically expire at or before EOL

prompt: A network architect is implementing an off-premises computing facility and needs to ensure that operation will not be impacted by major outages.
Which of the following should the architect consider?
explanation: A hot site is a fully equipped backup facility that can immediately take over operations in case of a major outage, making it the best choice for ensuring an off-premises computing facility will not be impacted by major outages. It provides real-time failover capability.

why.B: DCI (Data Center Interconnect) is about connecting data centers but doesn't inherently provide protection against major outages
why.C: Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection service, not a disaster recovery approach
why.D: Active-passive approach requires manual failover and doesn't guarantee uninterrupted operation

prompt: A network engineer is testing a website to ensure it is compatible with IPv6. After attempting to ping the website by its IPv6 address, the engineer determines that the DNS has not been set up properly.
Which of the following should the network engineer complete to resolve this issue?
explanation: To enable IPv6 DNS resolution, an AAAA record (not AAA) must be added to DNS. The AAAA record maps a domain name to its IPv6 address, allowing DNS to properly resolve
IPv6 addresses for the website.

why.A: PTR records are for reverse DNS lookups, not for enabling forward IPv6 resolution
why.B: TXT records store text information and are not used for IPv6 address resolution
why.D: Secondary NS records are for nameserver redundancy, not for IPv6 address resolution

prompt: A small coffee shop wants to set up multiple 2.4GHz wireless access points. The access points will support a large number of users, and the network technician wants to mitigate interference as much as possible.
Which of the following is the number of 22MHz channels that the equipment can support?
explanation: The 2.4GHz WiFi band has 11 available channels (1-11 in most regions), but only 3 non-overlapping channels can be used simultaneously when using 22MHz channels: channels 1, 6, and 11. These channels are spaced 25MHz apart, preventing interference with adjacent APs.

why.A: One channel is insufficient for multiple access points with interference mitigation
why.B: Two channels do not provide optimal spacing; only three channels can truly operate without overlap
why.D: Four non-overlapping 22MHz channels cannot fit in the 2.4GHz band; only three are available

prompt: A company is purchasing a 40Gbps broadband connection service from an ISP.
Which of the following should most likely be configured on the 10G switch to take advantage of the new service?
explanation: To take advantage of a 40Gbps broadband connection on a 10G switch, link aggregation must be configured to bond multiple 10Gbps ports together. This combines the bandwidth of multiple physical ports to create a 40Gbps logical connection.

why.A: 802.11Q tagging is for VLAN configuration, not for increasing bandwidth capacity
why.B: Jumbo frames increase frame size but do not add bandwidth capacity needed for 40Gbps service
why.C: Half duplex reduces throughput and is obsolete; full duplex is used in modern networks

prompt: Which of the following are the main differences between ESP and AH? (Choose two.)

options.text: AH provides confidentiality through the use of encryption.
ESP provides authentication for IP headers and their payloads.
ESP provides confidentiality through the use of encryption.
AH provides authentication for IP headers and their payloads.
AH provides data origin authorization over shared secret.
ESP provides data origin authorization over shared secret.

answerText: ESP provides confidentiality through the use of encryption.; AH provides authentication for IP headers and their payloads.
explanation: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) provides confidentiality through encryption of data, while AH (Authentication Header) provides authentication for IP headers and their payloads without encryption. These are the primary technical differences between the two IPsec protocols.

why.A: AH provides authentication, not confidentiality through encryption
why.B: AH provides authentication for IP headers and payloads, but ESP (not AH) also covers payloads
why.E: AH does not provide data origin authorization over shared secret; it uses HMAC for authentication
why.F: ESP does not provide data origin authorization over shared secret in the way this implies

prompt: An organization wants to ensure that incoming emails were sent from a trusted source.
Which of the following DNS records is used to verify the source?
explanation: TXT records are used to store email authentication information such as SPF (Sender Policy Framework), DKIM, and DMARC signatures. These records verify that incoming emails were sent from trusted sources by confirming the sender's authorization.

why.B: AAA records are used for IPv6 address resolution, not email authentication
why.C: CNAME records create aliases for domain names, not used for email source verification
why.D: MX records identify mail exchange servers but do not verify the source of incoming emails

prompt: Which of the following is the most closely associated with segmenting compute resources within a single cloud account?
explanation: A VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is the primary mechanism for segmenting compute resources within a single cloud account. It provides logical isolation of cloud resources, allowing users to define their own network topology, IP address ranges, and security policies. Network security groups operate at a lower layer for traffic filtering, IaaS is a service model, and hybrid cloud refers to multi-environment deployments.

why.A: Network security groups filter traffic but don't segment the compute resources themselves.
why.B: IaaS is a service delivery model, not a segmentation mechanism.
why.D: Hybrid cloud involves multiple environments, not segmentation within a single account.

prompt: Which of the following is the most likely function to be decremented when a tool is used to measure the distance between two locations on the internet?
explanation: TTL (Time To Live) is decremented by one each time a packet passes through a router hop. Tools that measure distance between internet locations, such as traceroute, use TTL to determine the number of hops and identify the path taken. GRE is a tunneling protocol, VPN is a security technology, and QoS relates to traffic prioritization.

why.A: GRE is a tunneling encapsulation protocol, not related to hop counting.
why.C: VPN is a security and privacy technology, not a hop metric.
why.D: QoS manages traffic prioritization and quality parameters, not hop distance.

prompt: A user's home mesh wireless network is experiencing latency issues. A technician has:
•  Performed a speed test.
•  Rebooted the devices.
•  Performed a site survey.
•  Performed a wireless packet capture.
The technician reviews the following information:
The technician notices in the packet capture that frames were retransmitted.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the user's network issue?

options.text: The SSIDs should not be the same.
The network has too much overlap.
The devices are incompatible with the mesh network.

answerText: The network has too much overlap.
explanation: The site survey data shows three mesh nodes all on the same channel (11) with overlapping coverage areas indicated by their similar RSSI values (-83dBm, -91dBm, -70dBm). When multiple access points operate on the same channel in close proximity with significant overlap, they create interference and collisions, causing frames to be retransmitted. This overlap is the primary cause of the latency issues. The solution would be to separate the nodes across non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 13 for 2.4GHz) or adjust their placement to reduce coverage overlap.

why.A: Having the same SSID for mesh nodes is correct practice for seamless roaming; identical SSIDs enable the mesh network to function properly.
why.C: If devices were incompatible with the mesh network, they likely would not connect at all rather than experience retransmissions indicating connection issues.
why.D: Underpowered nodes would show weak signal strength across all readings, but these RSSI values (-70 to -91dBm) indicate reasonable signal strength, not a power delivery problem.

prompt: A network engineer implements a 192.168.100.0/25 subnet for a building without obtaining sizing requirements. It is later determined that the building will house 700 people.
Which of the following subnet masks will most efficiently support that number of people?
explanation: A /25 subnet provides 126 usable hosts, insufficient for 700 people. A 255.255.252.0 (/22) subnet provides 1,022 usable hosts, which efficiently supports 700 people while minimizing wasted addresses. The /24 and /25 masks provide only 254 and 126 hosts respectively, while /23 (255.255.254.0) provides 510 hosts, which is also insufficient.

why.B: 255.255.254.0 (/23) provides only 510 usable hosts, insufficient for 700 people.
why.C: 255.255.255.0 (/24) provides only 254 usable hosts, insufficient for 700 people.
why.D: 255.255.255.128 (/25) provides only 126 usable hosts, insufficient for 700 people.

prompt: A company is building a new campus that will have wired and wireless devices. The network will be designed to support casual internet usage for guests and break rooms for employees.
Which of the following authentication methods is best suited for guests given the requirements of this scenario?
explanation: PSK (Pre-Shared Key) is the best suited authentication method for guest networks in this scenario. It allows simple, easy setup where guests receive a common passphrase without requiring individual credentials or complex infrastructure. ESP is an encryption protocol, WPA is an overall security standard (which uses PSK), and IKE is for VPN key exchange.

why.A: ESP is an encryption protocol, not an authentication method for wireless guests.
why.C: WPA is a security standard that can use PSK, but PSK itself is the authentication method.
why.D: IKE is used for VPN key negotiation, not wireless guest authentication.

prompt: Following the troubleshooting methodology, a technician implements a solution that resolves the reported issue.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: According to standard troubleshooting methodology, after implementing and verifying a solution works, the technician must document the findings. This step captures the problem, solution, and resolution for future reference and knowledge management. The other steps (creating plan, establishing theory, identifying problem) all precede the implementation phase.

why.B: Creating a plan of action occurs before implementation, not after.
why.C: Establishing a theory occurs during diagnosis, before implementing a solution.
why.D: Identifying the problem is the first step, completed long before solution implementation.

prompt: A network administrator needs to divide 192.168.1.0/24 into two equal halves.
Which of the following subnet masks should the administrator use?
explanation: To divide 192.168.1.0/24 into two equal halves, the administrator must change the prefix from /24 to /25, which is represented by the subnet mask 255.255.255.128. Each /25 subnet will contain 126 usable hosts and creates two equal divisions of the original /24 network.

why.A: 255.255.0.0 (/16) is a much larger mask that would encompass the entire network.
why.B: 255.255.254.0 (/23) combines two /24 networks, not dividing one.
why.C: 255.255.255.0 (/24) is the original mask, not a division of it.

prompt: Which of the following protocols uses the Dijkstra's Link State Algorithm to establish routes inside its routing table?
explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) uses Dijkstra's Link State Algorithm to calculate the shortest path and build its routing table. This algorithm evaluates all available paths and selects the most efficient route based on cost metrics. EIGRP uses a proprietary algorithm, BGP uses path-vector logic, and RIP uses distance-vector metrics.

why.B: EIGRP uses a proprietary Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL), not Dijkstra's algorithm.
why.C: BGP uses a path-vector algorithm based on autonomous system paths.
why.D: RIP uses a distance-vector algorithm based on hop count.

prompt: Which of the following traffic types does a DHCP Discover request from a PC use?
explanation: A DHCP Discover request uses broadcast traffic because the client does not yet know the DHCP server's address. The broadcast address ensures all devices on the local network segment receive the request, allowing any DHCP server to respond. Anycast, unicast, and multicast all require known addresses or specific routing configurations not available during initial DHCP discovery.

why.B: Anycast requires routing to the nearest instance of a service, unsuitable for discovery.
why.C: Unicast requires a known destination address, which the client lacks during discovery.
why.D: Multicast uses specific group addresses, not used for general DHCP discovery.

prompt: A user’s VoIP phone and workstation are connected through an inline cable. The user reports that the VoIP phone intermittently reboots, but the workstation is not having any network-related issues.
Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.text: The PoE power budget is exceeded.
The Ethernet cable is not working.

answerText: The PoE power budget is exceeded.
explanation: When a VoIP phone is connected inline with a workstation, the switch must provide Power over Ethernet (PoE) to the phone. If the PoE power budget is exceeded—meaning the switch cannot supply enough power to all connected devices—the phone may experience intermittent reboots as it loses and regains power. Since the workstation has no network issues, it's not a cable or signal problem, and port security wouldn't cause reboots.

why.B: Port security violations cause port shutdown or access denial, not intermittent device reboots.
why.C: Signal degradation would affect both the phone and workstation network connectivity equally.
why.D: A non-functional cable would prevent network communication entirely, not cause intermittent reboots.

prompt: A network administrator is installing a network for a small company. The switches will be installed in parallel to provide redundancy in case a specific device fails.
Which of the following should be configured to prevent loops?
explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is specifically designed to prevent loops in redundant network topologies by intelligently blocking certain paths while keeping others active, ensuring only one active path exists between any two network segments. When switches are installed in parallel for redundancy, STP detects and blocks redundant paths to prevent broadcast storms and loops.

why.B: CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) detects data corruption, not network loops.
why.C: Jumbo frames increase the maximum frame size for performance, not loop prevention.
why.D: Link aggregation combines multiple links for bandwidth, but doesn't prevent loops without STP.

prompt: A company’s network is experiencing high latency and packet loss during peak hours. Network monitoring tools show increased traffic on a switch.
Which of the following should a network technician implement to reduce the network congestion and improve performance?
explanation: Load balancing distributes network traffic across multiple paths or devices, directly reducing congestion on any single switch and improving overall network performance during peak hours. This addresses the root cause of the high latency and packet loss by preventing bottlenecks on the congested switch.

why.B: Port mirroring copies traffic for monitoring purposes but doesn't reduce congestion.
why.C: QoS prioritizes certain traffic types but doesn't reduce overall congestion if the total bandwidth is exceeded.
why.D: Spanning Tree Protocol prevents loops but doesn't address congestion or improve performance.

prompt: Which of the following VPN types provides secure remote access to the network resources through a web portal?
explanation: A clientless VPN (also called browser-based or web-based VPN) provides secure remote access to network resources through a web portal without requiring software installation on the client device. Users simply log in through a browser to access protected resources.

why.A: A proxy acts as an intermediary for requests but is not a VPN type for remote access.
why.C: Site-to-site VPN connects entire networks together, not individual users via web portal.
why.D: Direct connect is a dedicated network connection, not a VPN technology.

prompt: Which of the following best explains the role of confidentiality with regard to data at rest?

options.text: Data can be accessed by anyone on the administrative network.
Data can be accessed remotely with proper training.
Data can be accessed after privileged access is granted.
Data can be accessed after verifying the hash.

answerText: Data can be accessed after privileged access is
explanation: granted.

Confidentiality with regard to data at rest means that stored data is protected and can only be accessed by authorized individuals who have been granted appropriate privileges and permissions. This ensures that sensitive information remains secure and inaccessible to unauthorized users.

why.A: Confidentiality restricts access; it doesn't allow anyone on the administrative network to access data.
why.B: Remote access with training relates to authentication and authorization, not the core definition of confidentiality.
why.D: Hash verification ensures data integrity, not confidentiality.

prompt: Several users in an organization report connectivity issues and lag during a video meeting. The network administrator performs a tcpdump and observes increased retransmissions for other non-video applications on the network.
Which of the following symptoms describes the users' reported issues?
explanation: Packet loss is evidenced by increased retransmissions, as observed in the tcpdump results. When packets are lost, TCP protocols automatically retransmit them, causing the symptoms of lag and connectivity issues. Packet loss is the direct cause of the retransmissions detected by the monitoring tool.

why.A: Latency refers to delay but is not directly indicated by increased retransmissions alone.
why.C: Bottlenecking describes a resource constraint but the question specifically indicates retransmissions, which indicate packet loss.
why.D: Jitter is variation in latency, not the cause of increased retransmissions.

prompt: An administrator enables DNS filtering on the firewall to block users from visiting malicious websites.
Which of the following should the administrator also do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Disable DoH in users’ internet browsers.
Update NS record to point to DNS filter servers.
Block port 443 to the malicious websites.
Block port 53 to servers on the internet.
Disable TLS v1.3 in users’ internet browsers.

answerText: Disable DoH in users’ internet browsers.; Block port 53 to servers on the internet.
explanation: To ensure DNS filtering is effective, the administrator should disable DoH (DNS over HTTPS) in browsers, which bypasses DNS filtering by encrypting DNS queries directly to external resolvers, and block port 53 to external internet servers to prevent users from using alternative DNS servers that bypass the corporate filter. Option A prevents circumvention via encrypted DNS, and option D prevents direct DNS queries to non-filtered servers.

why.B: NS records point to authoritative nameservers; updating them doesn't enhance DNS filtering enforcement.
why.C: Blocking port 443 affects HTTPS traffic generally, not DNS filtering specifically.
why.E: TLS version disabling doesn't prevent DNS filtering bypass; DoH is the primary concern.
why.F: DNSSEC validates authenticity but doesn't enforce the DNS filter policy.

prompt: Which of the following is concerned with guaranteed availably of a cloud resource?
explanation: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is a contract that guarantees the availability and performance of cloud resources, specifying uptime percentages and compensation if those guarantees are not met. It directly addresses the guaranteed availability concern for cloud services.

why.A: IPAM (IP Address Management) manages IP address allocation, not availability guarantees.
why.C: MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) is a reliability metric but doesn't guarantee availability in contractual terms.
why.D: EOL (End of Life) indicates when a product is no longer supported, not availability guarantees.

prompt: A network consultant needs to decide between running an Ethernet uplink or using the built-in 5GHz point-to-point functionality on a WAP.
Which of the following documents provides the best information to assist the consultant with this decision?
explanation: A site survey provides empirical data about RF coverage, signal strength, interference patterns, and dead zones across the physical location. This data is essential to determine if wireless point-to-point functionality will have adequate coverage and performance compared to a wired Ethernet uplink, making it the best document to inform this decision.

why.B: Physical diagrams show layout but not RF propagation, signal strength, or interference data needed for this decision.
why.C: SLAs specify performance requirements but don't provide the technical RF measurements needed to choose between uplink options.
why.D: Logical diagrams show network topology and devices but lack the RF coverage and interference data critical to this decision.

prompt: While troubleshooting connectivity issues, a junior network administrator is given explicit instructions to test the host’s TCP/IP stack first.
Which of the following commands should the network administrator run?
explanation: The loopback address 127.0.0.1 is reserved for testing the local host's TCP/IP stack functionality. Pinging this address confirms that the network stack is properly installed and functioning on the device itself, independent of any network connectivity or external
devices.

why.B: 169.254.1.1 is in the link-local range and tests network connectivity, not the TCP/IP stack itself.
why.C: 172.16.1.1 is a private address and requires network connectivity to test, not the local stack.
why.D: 192.168.1.1 is a private address and requires network connectivity to test, not the local stack.

prompt: Users at an organization report that the wireless network is not working in some areas of the building. Users report that other wireless network SSIDs are visible when searching for the network, but the organization’s network is not displayed.
Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: If other SSIDs are visible but the organization's network is not displayed in affected areas, the issue is insufficient wireless coverage in those zones. The fact that competing networks are visible rules out interference/channel overlap as the primary cause and indicates the organization's WAPs simply don't reach those areas.

why.A: If interference or channel overlap were the issue, the organization's SSID would still be visible; it would just have poor performance.
why.C: Roaming misconfiguration affects handoffs between APs, not the initial visibility of the SSID.
why.D: Client disassociation issues cause drops after connection, not the absence of the SSID in scanning results.

prompt: Which of the following panels would be best to facilitate a central termination point for all network cables on the floor of a company building?
explanation: A patch panel provides the central termination point for all network cables on a floor, allowing organized cable management and easy reconfiguration of connections. While an MDF serves as the main distribution frame for the entire building, a patch panel is the most direct and common answer for facilitating central termination on a single floor.

why.B: A UPS provides backup power, not cable termination.
why.C: An MDF is the main distribution frame for the entire building; a patch panel is more appropriate for a single floor's central termination.
why.D: A rack is an equipment enclosure, not specifically designed as a termination point for network cables.

prompt: Which of the following is most commonly associated with many systems sharing one IP address in the public IP-addressing space?
explanation: Port Address Translation (PAT) is the technique most commonly used to allow many systems on a private network to share a single public IP address by translating both IP addresses and port numbers. This is the standard method used in most small office and home networks.

why.B: NAT translates addresses but doesn't typically involve port translation and is less efficient for many-to-one scenarios.
why.C: VIP (Virtual IP) is used for load balancing and failover, not for sharing a public address across many systems.
why.D: NAT64 is specifically for IPv6-to-IPv4 translation, not for many-to-one public address sharing.

prompt: A network administrator is reviewing a production web server and observes the following output from the netstat command:
Which of the following actions should the network administrator take to harden the security of the web server?
explanation: The netstat output shows multiple TCP ports in LISTENING state on the web server (ports 1308, 329, 758, 1459, 1245, 392, 43, 43). For a production web server, only necessary ports should be open (typically HTTP port 80 and HTTPS port 443). All other listening ports represent unnecessary services that increase the attack surface. Disabling these unused ports is a fundamental hardening practice that reduces potential vulnerabilities and exposure to exploitation.

why.B: Access control lists help restrict who can access open ports, but don't address the core issue of unnecessary services listening on unused ports.
why.C: Content filtering operates at the application layer and is irrelevant to the presence of unnecessary listening ports at the network level.
why.D: A screened subnet (DMZ) is a network architecture decision that doesn't directly address unnecessary open ports on an individual server.

prompt: A network technician is examining the configuration on an access port and notices more than one VLAN has been set.
Which of the following best describes how the port is configured?
explanation: An access port configured with more than one VLAN indicates a voice VLAN setup, where the port carries both data traffic on one VLAN and voice traffic on another VLAN simultaneously. This is a standard configuration for IP phones and other devices requiring separate voice and data streams.

why.B: Access ports are designed to carry one VLAN; having multiple VLANs is not a misconfiguration but rather the intended voice VLAN design.
why.C: A default VLAN is a single VLAN assigned by default; this doesn't explain multiple VLANs on the port.
why.D: A native VLAN applies to trunk ports for untagged traffic, not to access ports with multiple VLANs.

prompt: A small company has the following IP addressing strategy:
•  Voice subnet: 192.168.2.0/24
•  Server subnet: 192 168.10.0/24
A user is unable to connect to the company fileshare server located at 192.168.10.1. The user's networking configuration is:
Which of the following will most likely correct the issue?

options.text: Changing the DNS servers to internet IPs

explanation: The user's IP address is 192.168.1.x with a subnet mask of 255.255.0.0, which places them in the 192.168.0.0/16 network. However, the server is at 192.168.10.1. With the current /16 subnet mask, the user's device would think 192.168.10.1 is on the same subnet and attempt direct communication. The correct subnet mask for the user subnet should be 255.255.255.0 (/24), which properly segments the network so that 192.168.10.1 is recognized as a different subnet, requiring routing through the default gateway (192.168.1.200) to reach the server.

why.A: The user's IP address (192.168.1.x) is correct for the user subnet; changing it to the server's address would create a conflict.
why.C: The DNS servers listed (192.168.10.10 and 192.168.10.11) are internal servers appropriate for the company network, not internet IPs.
why.D: The physical (MAC) address has no bearing on routing between different subnets; it only matters for local subnet communication.

prompt: A network administrator needs to connect a department to a new network segment. They need to use a DHCP server located on another network.
Which of the following can the administrator use to complete this task?
explanation: An IP Helper (DHCP relay) forwards DHCP requests from clients on one network segment to a DHCP server located on a different network segment. This allows a new department to obtain IP addresses from a centralized DHCP server without requiring a local DHCP server on their network.

why.B: A reservation statically assigns an IP to a specific client; it doesn't solve the problem of reaching a remote DHCP server.
why.C: An exclusion removes addresses from a scope but doesn't enable communication with a remote DHCP server.
why.D: A scope defines the range of addresses a DHCP server distributes but doesn't enable reaching a server on another network.

prompt: A network engineer is implementing a solution by which on-premises servers are migrated to a cloud service provider.
Which of the following service models will provide a lift and shift solution to meet this requirement?
explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides virtualized computing resources over the internet and enables lift-and-shift migrations where on-premises servers are migrated to cloud-based virtual machines with minimal modification, preserving the existing OS and application stack.

why.B: Infrastructure as code is a methodology for defining infrastructure through code; it doesn't represent a cloud service model for server migration.
why.C: Software as a Service (SaaS) provides fully managed applications in the cloud, not the underlying infrastructure for migrating existing servers.
why.D: Software-defined networking is a networking architecture approach, not a cloud service model for server migration.

prompt: A network administrator is conducting an assessment and found network devices that do not meet standards.
Which of the following configurations is considered a set of rules that devices should adhere to?
explanation: A golden configuration (or golden image) is a set of standard settings and rules that

network devices should adhere to. It serves as the baseline configuration template that all devices must follow to meet organizational standards. Production refers to live environments, backup refers to data copies, and candidate refers to configurations being tested but not yet approved.

why.A: Production is an environment state, not a set of standards rules.
why.B: Backup refers to data protection and recovery, not configuration standards.
why.C: Candidate configurations are being evaluated but not yet the official standard.

prompt: An IT department asks a newly hired employee to use a personal laptop until the company can provide one.
Which of the following policies is most applicable to this situation?
explanation: BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) is the policy that explicitly addresses employees using personal devices for work purposes. This policy covers the terms under which employees can use their own laptops, phones, or other devices to access company resources and networks. IAM governs identity management, DLP prevents data loss, and AUP defines acceptable use but doesn't specifically address personal device usage.

why.A: IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls authentication and authorization, not personal device usage.
why.C: DLP (Data Loss Prevention) prevents unauthorized data movement, not personal device policies.
why.D: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) defines general usage rules but doesn't specifically address personal device scenarios.

prompt: Which of the following offers the ability to manage access at the cloud VM instance?
explanation: A security group is a cloud-based firewall mechanism that manages access at the cloud VM instance level by controlling inbound and outbound traffic. It operates at Layer 4 (transport) and can be configured to restrict traffic to specific ports, protocols, and sources. Internet gateways provide external connectivity, Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connections, and Network ACLs operate at the subnet level rather than instance level.

why.B: An Internet gateway provides external connectivity, not instance-level access management.
why.C: Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between on-premises and cloud, not instance-level access control.
why.D: Network ACLs operate at the subnet level, not at the individual VM instance level.

prompt: In an environment with one router, which of the following will allow a network engineer to communicate between VLANs without purchasing additional hardware?
explanation: Subinterfaces allow a single physical router interface to be divided into multiple logical interfaces, each assigned to a different VLAN. This enables inter-VLAN routing without requiring additional hardware. VXLAN is for overlay networks over larger distances, a Layer 3 switch would require purchasing hardware which is prohibited by the scenario, and VIP is a load balancing concept.

why.B: VXLAN is designed for large-scale network overlays, not single-router VLAN routing.
why.C: A Layer 3 switch would accomplish the goal but requires purchasing additional hardware, which the scenario prohibits.
why.D: VIP (Virtual IP) is used for load balancing and redundancy, not inter-VLAN communication.

prompt: A network administrator is concerned with on-path attacks and wants to provide encryption of fully qualified domain names in outbound communications.
Which of the following best describes the protocol that provides the proper security layer for internet communication?
explanation: DoH (DNS over HTTPS) specifically encrypts fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) in DNS queries by tunneling them through HTTPS. This prevents on-path attackers from viewing what domains are being queried. SSL/TLS are general encryption protocols, and DNSSEC provides authentication rather than encryption of the DNS queries themselves.

why.A: SSL is a general encryption protocol not specifically designed for DNS query encryption.
why.C: TLS is a general encryption protocol but DoH is the specific protocol that encrypts DNS queries over HTTPS.
why.D: DNSSEC provides authentication and integrity verification of DNS data, not encryption of the queries themselves.

prompt: A network administrator wants to restrict inbound traffic to allow only HTTPS to the company website, denying all other inbound traffic from the internet.
Which of the following would best accomplish this goal?

options.text: Port security on an access switch
Content filtering on a web gateway
URL filtering on an outbound proxy

explanation: An ACL (Access Control List) on the edge firewall is the appropriate tool for controlling inbound internet traffic at the perimeter. It can be configured to allow only HTTPS (port 443) traffic to the web server while denying all other inbound traffic. Port security operates on access switches for local network protection, content filtering examines content types,
and URL filtering is for outbound proxy traffic, not inbound internet restrictions.

why.B: Port security on access switches protects local network segments, not inbound internet traffic.
why.C: Content filtering examines the content of traffic but doesn't restrict based on ports for inbound access control.
why.D: URL filtering on outbound proxies controls outbound web access, not inbound internet traffic restrictions.

prompt: A network engineer is deploying switches at a new remote office. The switches have been preconfigured with hostnames and STP priority values.
Based on the following table:
Which of the following switches will become the root bridge?
explanation: In Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), the root bridge is elected based on the lowest bridge priority value. Examining the table, core-sw01 has a priority of 4096, access-sw01 has 4096, distribution-sw01 has 32768, and access-sw02 has 32768. Both core-sw01 and access-sw01 share the lowest priority of 4096, so the tiebreaker is the MAC address—the switch with the lowest MAC address becomes root bridge. Core-sw01's MAC address (0000.0000.005f) is lower than access-sw01's MAC address (0000.0000.005e), so core-sw01 becomes the root bridge.

why.B: access-sw01 has priority 4096 but its MAC address (0000.0000.005e) is higher than core-sw01's (0000.0000.005f), so it loses the tiebreaker.
why.C: distribution-sw01 has priority 32768, which is higher than the lowest priority of 4096.
why.D: access-sw02 has priority 32768, which is higher than the lowest priority of 4096.

prompt: Which of following must be implemented to securely connect a company’s headquarters with a branch location?
explanation: A site-to-site VPN securely connects two fixed network locations (headquarters and branch) by establishing an encrypted tunnel between the networks. This allows both locations to communicate securely as if they were on the same network. Split-tunnel and full-tunnel VPNs are client-based remote access solutions, and clientless VPN enables browser-based access, not site-to-site office connectivity.

why.A: Split-tunnel VPN is a client-based remote access configuration, not a site-to-site solution.
why.B: Clientless VPN provides browser-based access for individual remote users, not office-to-office connectivity.
why.C: Full-tunnel VPN is a client-based remote access configuration, not a permanent site-to-site connection.

prompt: A network engineer needs to virtualize network services, including a router, at a remote branch location.
Which of the following solutions meets the requirements?
explanation: NFV (Network Function Virtualization) enables the virtualization of network services and

functions, including routers, firewalls, and other network appliances, on standard hardware at remote locations. This allows a branch to have virtualized network services without dedicated hardware. VRF is for routing isolation, VLAN is for network segmentation, and VPC is for cloud infrastructure, none of which specifically virtualize network functions like routers.

why.B: VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) provides routing isolation but doesn't virtualize network services.
why.C: VLAN provides network segmentation but doesn't virtualize network functions like routers.
why.D: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a cloud infrastructure concept, not a solution for virtualizing network services at branch locations.

prompt: A group of users cannot connect to network resources. The technician runs ipconfig from one user's device and is able to ping the gateway shown from the command.
Which of the following is most likely preventing the users from accessing network resources?
explanation: The user has a valid IP configuration (can ping gateway), but cannot access network resources. This indicates the device received an IP address but cannot reach other resources. A rogue DHCP server would assign IPs that appear valid locally but prevent access to actual network resources by pointing clients to incorrect gateways or DNS servers. VLAN hopping and Evil twin require different attack vectors, and DDoS would affect multiple systems differently.

why.A: VLAN hopping requires switch exploitation and would not allow the device to function with a valid gateway IP.
why.C: DDoS affects availability globally and would show different symptoms across the network.
why.D: Evil twin is a wireless attack and wouldn't prevent access when the device already has a valid IP configuration.

prompt: Which of the following disaster recovery concepts is calculated by dividing the total hours of operation by the total number of units?
explanation: MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) is calculated as total hours of operation divided by total number of failures. This metric represents the average time expected before a system fails. MTTR measures repair time, RPO measures data loss tolerance, and RTO measures system recovery time—none of these use the hours/units formula described.

why.A: MTTR (Mean Time To Repair) is calculated as total downtime divided by number of failures, not total hours of operation by units.
why.C: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) is a time measurement for acceptable data loss, not calculated this way.
why.D: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) is the target time to restore service, not calculated by this formula.

prompt: A network administrator has been monitoring the company’s servers to ensure that they are available.
Which of the following should the administrator use for this task?
explanation: SNMP traps are automated alerts that network devices send to a management station when specific conditions occur. They are the standard tool for proactive server and device monitoring to ensure availability. Packet capture is for traffic analysis, data usage reports track bandwidth, and configuration monitoring tracks changes—none directly monitor availability.

why.A: Packet capture analyzes traffic patterns but does not monitor server availability.
why.B: Data usage reports track bandwidth consumption, not server availability status.
why.D: Configuration monitoring tracks configuration changes, not whether servers are available and operational.

prompt: A network engineer is completing a wireless installation in a new building. A requirement is that all clients be able to automatically connect to the fastest supported network.
Which of the following best supports this requirement?
explanation: Band steering automatically directs clients to the fastest available network band (typically 5GHz over 2.4GHz) without manual intervention. This ensures all clients connect optimally while maintaining a single SSID. Disabling 5GHz would eliminate the faster band entirely, captive portals are for authentication, and MAC filtering is for access control.

why.B: Disabling 5GHz prevents clients from connecting to the fastest network, defeating the requirement.
why.C: Captive portals handle authentication and login, not automatic selection of fastest networks.
