steps: 1. Note from the topology that PC 3 sits in VLAN 10 on Switch 1 while the file, database and web servers sit in VLAN 20 on Switch 2.
2. Because PC 3 still reaches the internet through Switch 1's Gi6 uplink, its own VLAN and access port are healthy, so the fault is on the path between the two switches.
3. The only link between the switches is Gi1 to Gi1, so that interface must be a trunk carrying both VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 traffic.

4. Enter interface gi1, set switchport mode trunk, allow VLANs 10 and 20, and end the configuration on Switch 1, then repeat the identical commands on Switch 2 since a trunk must be configured on both ends.
5. Return to PC 3 and ping 192.168.1.30 (file server) and 192.168.1.32 (web server); replies with 0% loss confirm the trunk now carries VLAN 20.

PC 3 can reach the internet, which proves its access port, IP settings and VLAN 10 on Switch 1 are fine. What fails is only traffic that has to cross from Switch 1 to Switch 2, where the VLAN 20 servers live. The single Gi1-to-Gi1 cable between the switches was not carrying the needed VLANs, so frames tagged for VLAN 20 (and VLAN 10) were dropped. Configuring Gi1 on each switch as a trunk and explicitly permitting VLANs 10 and 20 lets tagged traffic for both VLANs traverse the link; a trunk has to be set identically on both ends, which is why the same four commands are entered on Switch 1 and Switch 2. Afterwards, pinging 192.168.1.30 and 192.168.1.32 from PC 3 validates the fix — successful replies with 0% packet loss show inter-switch VLAN connectivity is restored.

prompt: A network administrator has been tasked with configuring a network for a new corporate office. The office consists of two buildings, separated by 50 feet with no physical connectivity. The configuration must meet the following requirements:
•  Devices in both buildings should be able to access the Internet.
•  Security insists that all Internet traffic be inspected before entering the network.
•  Desktops should not see traffic destined for other devices.
•  All core networking devices need to be managed within Building A.
INSTRUCTIONS
Select the appropriate network device for each location. If applicable, click on the magnifying glass next to any device which may require configuration updates and make any necessary changes.
Not all devices will be used, but all locations should be filled.
summary: Drag the correct network device onto each of the five unknown placeholders in the two-
building topology so all requirements are met.

pairs.item: Placeholder in Building A (top left, above desktops)

steps: 1. Because the desktops in Building A must not see one another's traffic, the device aggregating them has to segment traffic per port, so a switch (not a hub) is placed in Building A.
2. Security requires all Internet traffic to be inspected before entering the network, so the device directly facing the Internet cloud is the firewall.
3. Behind the firewall a router is needed to route between the internal networks and perform NAT for outbound Internet access.
4. With 50 feet and no physical cabling between the buildings, a wireless bridge is required: a WAP in Building A radiates the wireless network.
5. In Building B a wireless range extender associates with the Building A WAP and rebroadcasts the signal to the laptops and mobile device, keeping all core managed devices in Building A.

The topology is built from the Internet inward. The firewall sits at the very edge so every packet from the Internet is inspected before it can reach the corporate network, satisfying the security mandate. Behind it, the router provides routing and NAT between the internal segments and the outside world. In Building A the wired desktops connect to a switch, which forwards frames only to the port where the destination lives; a hub would flood every frame to all ports and would let desktops see each other's traffic, so it is deliberately left unused. Since the two buildings have no cabling between them, connectivity is achieved wirelessly: a WAP in Building A creates the wireless network, and a wireless range extender in Building B links back to that WAP and rebroadcasts the signal to the laptops and phone. All of the core devices (firewall, router, switch, WAP) remain in Building A, so they can be managed from there as required.

prompt: Users are reporting latency on the network. The network engineer notes the following:
•  Confirms the only change was a new network switch
•  Confirms all users are experiencing latency
•  Thinks the issue is a network loop caused by the lower bridge ID of the new switch
Which of the following describes the next step in the troubleshooting methodology?
explanation: The network engineer has already identified the problem (latency after new switch installation) and formed a theory (network loop caused by lower bridge ID). According to the standard troubleshooting methodology, the next step is to test the theory by validating whether a network loop actually exists and confirming the bridge ID is causing it.

why.A: The problem has already been identified; this step is complete.
why.C: Implementation comes after testing the theory, not before.
why.D: Verification of full system functionality occurs after implementing the solution.

prompt: A network technician needs to configure IP addressing in a Class C network with eight subnets total:
•  Three for 60 hosts
•  Three for 15 hosts
•  Two for seven hosts
Which of the following solutions should the technician use to accomplish this task?
explanation: VLSM (Variable Length Subnet Mask) allows different subnets to have different subnet mask lengths based on their host requirements. With three subnets needing 60 hosts (/26), three needing 15 hosts (/28), and two needing 7 hosts (/29), VLSM is the only method that efficiently allocates exactly the right amount of addresses for each subnet size within a single Class C network.

why.A: CIDR is a classless addressing notation but does not specifically describe the technique for creating subnets of varying sizes.
why.B: APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) is for automatic IP assignment when DHCP fails, not for planned subnet design.
why.D: RFC 1918 defines private IP address ranges, not a subnetting technique.

prompt: A user reports being unable to connect to an on-premises code repository. A systems administrator verifies that the repository is reachable from other devices.
Which of the following commands should the systems administrator use first to troubleshoot the issue with the user's device?
explanation: When a user cannot connect to a repository while others can, the first step should be to verify DNS resolution works on the user's device. nslookup is the primary tool to test whether the device can resolve the repository's hostname to an IP address. If DNS fails, the user cannot reach the repository regardless of network connectivity. This is the logical first troubleshooting step before testing routing (tracert) or packet analysis (tcpdump).

why.B: dig is also a DNS tool but nslookup is the standard first troubleshooting command on most systems.
why.C: tcpdump captures packets but requires knowing what traffic to look for; it's premature without confirming basic connectivity first.
why.D: tracert tests routing/path to a destination but should come after confirming DNS resolution works on the user's device.

prompt: A network administrator is verifying logical connectivity to a Layer 2 switch.
Which of the following addresses should the administrator issue the ping command to?
explanation: To ping a Layer 2 switch for logical connectivity verification, the administrator must ping an

IP address. MAC addresses cannot be pinged directly. An SVI (Switch Virtual Interface) is an IP interface on a VLAN that allows Layer 2 switches to have routable IP addresses for management purposes. This is the standard method for verifying connectivity to a Layer 2 switch.

why.A: MAC addresses are not routable and cannot be pinged; ping operates at Layer 3 using IP addresses.
why.B: A VIP (Virtual IP) is typically used for load balancing or failover, not for switch management access.
why.C: A WAN address would be used for external connectivity, not for verifying logical connectivity to a switch.

prompt: Which of the following standards enables the use of an enterprise authentication for network access control?
explanation: 802.1X is the IEEE standard for port-based network access control (PNAC) that enables enterprise authentication. It provides a framework for authenticating devices and users before granting network access, working with backend authentication servers like RADIUS or TACACS+. This is the standard specifically designed for network access control with enterprise authentication.

why.A: 802.1Q is for VLAN tagging, not authentication or access control.
why.C: 802.3bt is a Power over Ethernet (PoE) standard, not related to authentication.
why.D: 802.11h is a wireless standard for dynamic frequency selection and transmit power control, not enterprise authentication.

prompt: Which of the following enables an organization to leverage an identity provider to manage access across SaaS applications?
explanation: Single Sign-On (SSO) enables organizations to leverage an identity provider to manage access across multiple SaaS applications with a single set of credentials. Users authenticate once with the identity provider and gain access to all connected applications without re-authenticating. This is the core purpose and definition of SSO.

why.A: PKI (Public Key Infrastructure) manages digital certificates and encryption, not centralized identity management across SaaS applications.
why.C: TACACS+ is a network device authentication protocol, not designed for SaaS application access management.
why.D: RADIUS is primarily for network access authentication (Wi-Fi, VPN), not for managing SaaS application access through an identity provider.

prompt: Which of the following can manage, control, and assist with conditioning power within a data center?
explanation: A Power Distribution Unit (PDU) manages, controls, and conditions power within a data center by distributing electrical power to multiple devices, providing surge protection, monitoring capabilities, and often metering features. PDUs are fundamental infrastructure components that enable centralized power management and conditioning.

why.A: A power usage monitor only observes and reports power consumption; it does not manage or condition power.
why.B: A line voltage monitor only measures voltage levels; it does not manage or condition power.
why.C: An Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) provides backup power during outages but is not the primary tool for managing and conditioning power distribution throughout the data center.

prompt: A company lost the ability to connect to the internet at a satellite office. Logging tools capture the last recorded event as a login from the router's default credentials. The network administrator is unable to access the router.
Which of the following should the administrator do to prevent this issue in the future?

options.text: Change the name of the router.
Document the configuration of the router.
Modify the local username and password of the router.

answerText: Modify the local username and password of the
explanation: router.

The incident shows that default credentials on the router were compromised, allowing unauthorized access that disrupted connectivity. To prevent this in the future, the administrator must change the router's default username and password to custom credentials. This removes the most obvious attack vector and is a fundamental security practice.

why.A: Changing the router's name does not prevent unauthorized access via default credentials.
why.B: Documenting the configuration does not prevent security breaches from default credentials.
why.D: Installing a secondary router provides redundancy but does not address the root cause of the security vulnerability.

prompt: A company needs to add a new facility to its WAN, but connecting it via fiber is too expensive. The Chief Executive Officer decides to connect the new facility via radio.
Which of the following describes this type of network?
explanation: A point-to-point connection describes a direct link between two specific locations, which is exactly what connecting a new facility via radio represents—a dedicated wireless
connection between the main site and the new satellite facility. This is a standard point-to-point radio or microwave link deployment.

why.A: Hybrid networks combine multiple connection types (fiber, cable, wireless) typically across more than two sites.
why.B: Direct Connect usually refers to dedicated physical circuits or vendor-specific managed connections, not radio links.
why.C: Mesh networks involve multiple interconnected nodes with redundant paths; this single link to one new facility is not mesh topology.

prompt: An organization has a guest network with a network IP range of 192.168.1.0/28 using a DHCP pool. One visitor reported difficulties connecting and configured a static IP address. Following this action, another visitor reported intermittent connection issues.
Which of the following is the most likely reason for the intermittent connection issues?
explanation: A /28 subnet provides only 14 usable IP addresses (192.168.1.0/28 = .1 to .14). When one visitor manually configured a static IP from the same range without coordination with DHCP, that IP was likely already in the DHCP pool or subsequently assigned to another device. This creates duplicate IP addresses on the network, causing the second visitor's connection to fail intermittently due to address conflicts.

why.A: Address pool exhaustion would cause complete connection failure for new DHCP requests, not intermittent issues for existing connections.
why.C: Misconfigured default gateway would cause routing failure, not intermittent connectivity specifically tied to the second visitor's connection timing.
why.D: Incorrect subnet mask would prevent any connectivity on the subnet; it would not cause intermittent issues only after the static configuration.

prompt: A systems administrator is resolving connectivity issues to an organization’s DNS server. While troubleshooting, the administrator performs remote scans ana receives the following output:
Which or the following should the systems administrator investigate?
explanation: The output shows various TCP and UDP ports with their states (open, closed). The DNS server should have port 53/TCP and 53/UDP open for DNS queries, and both are shown as 'open'. However, other ports that should typically be closed or filtered are also appearing as open (21/TCP, 22/TCP, 69/TCP, 636/TCP, 6050/TCP), suggesting that firewall rules may not be properly configured to restrict access to only necessary services. Additionally, some expected services show as 'closed' (69/TCP, 6050/TCP, 8443/TCP), which could indicate incomplete firewall filtering. The administrator should investigate firewall rules to ensure only necessary DNS ports and services are exposed.

why.A: URL filters operate at the application layer and would not directly affect port-level connectivity shown in network scan results.
why.B: While unused services could be running, the scan output shows port states rather than running service information, making firewall rules the more immediate concern.
why.D: 802.1X is an authentication protocol for network access; the issue presents port accessibility states that point to firewall configuration rather than switch-level authentication problems.

prompt: A network administrator is implementing dynamic routing protocols for a large enterprise network that has several vendor devices.
Which of the following is the best choice for an enterprise network with multiple locations and high-bandwidth requirements?
explanation: OSPF is the best choice for large enterprise networks with multiple locations and high-bandwidth requirements. It is vendor-independent, scales well, converges quickly, supports equal-cost multipath (ECMP), and is widely deployed in enterprise environments. While IS-IS is also suitable, OSPF is more commonly used for internal routing in enterprises.

why.A: IS-IS, while viable for large networks, is less commonly deployed in enterprises than OSPF.
why.C: BGP is used for inter-AS (autonomous system) routing, not for intra-enterprise routing with high bandwidth.
why.D: RIP is outdated with severe limitations including maximum 15 hops and slow convergence, unsuitable for large networks.

prompt: A wireless administrator is setting up a small mesh network in an open-concept office space. The administrator must select a supported frequency that offers the fastest speeds for the backhaul connection.
Which of the following should the administrator select?
explanation: The diagram shows AP 1 using 802.11ac (WiFi 5) on 5GHz and AP 2 and AP 3 using 802.11ax (WiFi 6) on 6GHz. However, for backhaul connections in mesh networks, 5GHz (802.11ac/ax) provides the fastest practical speeds compared to 2.4GHz. While 6GHz offers additional spectrum, 5GHz is the established standard that offers the fastest speeds and best performance for backhaul in current mesh deployments. The question asks which frequency offers the fastest speeds for backhaul - 5GHz delivers superior throughput compared to 2.4GHz due to wider channel widths and higher data rates, making it the optimal choice for high-speed backhaul connections.

why.A: 2.4GHz offers significantly slower maximum speeds and more interference, making it unsuitable for high-speed backhaul connections.
why.C: While 6GHz is newer, backhaul optimization and the fastest supported speeds are better achieved on 5GHz for most mesh deployments.
why.D: 45GHz is not a supported WiFi frequency and does not exist in wireless standards.

prompt: A network administrator is looking for a single tool that will monitor both bandwidth utilization and interface status.
Which of the following best meets this requirement?
explanation: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) is specifically designed to monitor and manage network devices. It can collect both bandwidth utilization data and interface status information through MIBs (Management Information Bases), making it the single tool that best meets both requirements.

why.A: Nmap is a port scanner used for discovery and security auditing, not for continuous monitoring of bandwidth and interface status.
why.C: Packet capture analyzes traffic at the packet level but does not provide aggregated bandwidth utilization or interface status monitoring.
why.D: Syslog collects log messages from devices but is not designed to monitor real-time bandwidth utilization or interface metrics.

prompt: A network administrator is able to make changes to a network device using a specific, isolated port.
Which of the following most closely describes this management scheme?
explanation: Out-of-band management describes using a separate, isolated management network or port to access network devices, independent of the production network. This provides
secure, reliable access even when the main network is compromised or unavailable.

why.A: API is a programmatic interface for communication but does not specifically describe isolated port-based management.
why.C: A jump box is an intermediary host used to access other systems, but does not specifically describe an isolated port.
why.D: SSH is a protocol for secure remote access but does not inherently imply isolation or out-of-band connectivity.

prompt: Which of the following describes limiting access to tools or facilities based on job role?
explanation: The principle of least privilege means granting users and roles only the minimum access necessary to perform their job functions. This directly describes limiting access to tools and facilities based on job role, ensuring security by restricting unnecessary permissions.

why.B: ACL (Access Control List) is a technical mechanism for implementing access rules but is not a principle describing role-based limitations.
why.C: MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) is about verifying identity through multiple factors, not about limiting access based on job role.
why.D: An allow list is a technical implementation tool that specifies what is permitted, not the principle guiding why restrictions exist.

prompt: Which of the following methods is used to authenticate users and devices connecting to a network?
explanation: NAC (Network Access Control) is a security framework that authenticates both users and devices before allowing them to connect to a network. It verifies device compliance and user credentials, ensuring only authorized and compliant endpoints gain network access.

why.A: VLAN is used for network segmentation and isolation, not for authentication of users and devices.
why.B: ACL controls traffic flow based on defined rules but does not authenticate users or devices.
why.D: UTM (Unified Threat Management) provides security functions like filtering and threat prevention but is not the primary method for user/device authentication.

prompt: A customer wants to segment the local network into eight sections with 30 devices each. A junior network technician needs to select the appropriate subnet mask for the customer's chosen Class C network.
Which of the following meets the requirement?
explanation: To segment a Class C network into 8 sections with 30 devices each requires subnetting. With 30 devices per section, 5 bits are needed for host addresses (2^5 = 32 addresses, providing 30 usable). This leaves 3 bits for subnetting (2^3 = 8 subnets). A /27 subnet mask (255.255.255.224) provides exactly 8 subnets with 32 addresses (30 usable hosts) per subnet.

why.A: /25 provides only 2 subnets, insufficient for the requirement of 8 sections.
why.B: /26 provides 4 subnets, insufficient for the requirement of 8 sections.
why.D: /28 provides 16 subnets with 16 addresses each (14 usable hosts), which is more than needed and wastes addressing space.

prompt: Which of the following is the best reason to create a golden configuration?

options.text: To decrease the size of configuration files
To increase security by encrypting configurations
To set up backup configurations for each device

explanation: A golden configuration is a standardized, tested baseline configuration that serves as a template for deploying consistent settings across network devices. Its primary purpose is ensuring configuration consistency across the enterprise, which improves reliability, security, and manageability.

why.B: Golden configurations do not primarily aim to decrease file size; their focus is on standardization and consistency.
why.C: While security can be included in a golden configuration, encryption of configurations is not the primary reason for creating one.
why.D: Golden configurations establish standards for initial deployment, not specifically for creating backup configurations for each device.

prompt: A network engineer is providing basic, public network connectivity to a VPC.
Which of the following should the engineer implement?
explanation: An Internet Gateway is the appropriate AWS component for providing basic, public internet connectivity to a VPC. It enables resources within the VPC to communicate with the internet and allows external users to access public resources in the VPC.

why.A: Direct Connect is for dedicated, private network connections between on-premises infrastructure and AWS, not public internet connectivity.
why.B: Site-to-site VPN establishes encrypted connections between on-premises networks and VPCs, not public internet connectivity.
why.D: NFV (Network Function Virtualization) is a cloud infrastructure approach for virtualizing network services, not a mechanism for basic public connectivity.

prompt: Employees report that website requests are being redirected to other websites that display different content than expected.
Which of the following attacks is most likely causing this issue?
explanation: DNS poisoning occurs when an attacker corrupts DNS cache or responses, causing users to be redirected to malicious websites with different content than expected. This directly matches the symptom of website requests being redirected to unexpected content.

why.A: MAC flooding is a Layer 2 attack that overwhelms switch tables and causes flooding, not content redirection.
why.B: ARP spoofing redirects traffic at Layer 2 to intercept it, but doesn't change the content displayed by redirecting to different websites.
why.D: VLAN hopping allows unauthorized access between VLANs but doesn't cause website redirection to different content.

prompt: A global company has acquired a local company. The companies are geographically separate. The fully utilized IP address ranges for the two companies are as follows:
•  Global company: 10.0.0.0/16
•  Local company: 10.0.0.0/24
Which of the following can the network engineer do to quickly connect the two companies and minimize user disruption?

options.text: Assign static routing to advertise the local company's network.
Assign an overlapping IP address range to both companies.
Assign a new IP address range to the local company.
Assign a NAT range to the local company.

answerText: Assign a NAT range to the local company.
explanation: Using NAT on the local company's IP range allows the overlapping 10.0.0.0/24 network to be translated to a different address space for routing purposes, enabling quick connectivity without requiring IP re-addressing of fully-utilized networks. This minimizes disruption since existing devices don't need reconfiguration.

why.A: Static routing doesn't solve the overlapping IP address problem; traffic would still be ambiguous.
why.B: Assigning overlapping IP ranges would cause routing conflicts and is not a solution.
why.C: Reassigning a new IP range to the local company would cause significant user disruption and network reconfiguration.

prompt: An attacker remotely executes a binary file on a server.
Which of the following terms describes what the attacker is taking advantage of?
explanation: An exploit is a specific technique, tool, or code that takes advantage of a vulnerability to achieve unauthorized access or execution. In this scenario, the remote execution of a binary file is the exploit—the actual attack method being used.

why.A: A threat is a potential danger but not the specific method of attack.
why.B: A risk is the combination of threat and vulnerability; it's not the attack method itself.
why.C: A vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited, but the vulnerability itself isn't being taken advantage of—the exploit is.

prompt: A company experienced a breach and wants to implement preventive measures. The network administrator is looking for a tool that can collect, analyze, and quickly correlate known attacks.
Which of the following software tools can accomplish this task?
explanation: SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) tools collect, analyze, and correlate security events across multiple sources, including known attack patterns and signatures, making them ideal for detecting and responding to known attacks quickly.

why.A: Syslog collectors only aggregate logs from devices; they don't analyze or correlate known attacks.
why.C: Packet capture tools capture network traffic but don't inherently analyze or correlate known attack patterns.
why.D: SNMP traps are notifications from network devices but don't correlate known attacks or provide analysis.

prompt: Users are reporting issues with mobile phone connectivity after a cellular repeater was recently installed. Users also note that the phones are rapidly losing battery charge.
Which of the following should the technician check first to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: Signal strength should be checked first when users experience connectivity issues and battery drain after a cellular repeater installation. Poor signal strength forces phones to use more power searching for signals, causing rapid battery depletion, and the repeater may be improperly configured or positioned.

why.A: WPS is a Wi-Fi configuration feature, not relevant to cellular repeater issues.
why.C: Channel frequency is not the primary issue; cellular networks use specific frequencies allocated by carriers.
why.D: While power budget relates to signal strength, checking signal strength directly is the first diagnostic step.

prompt: Which of the following is an attack that provides a malicious default gateway IP over a wired network?
explanation: A rogue DHCP server is an attack that provides false network configuration, including a malicious default gateway IP address, over a wired network. This server responds to DHCP requests faster than legitimate servers, poisoning clients with attackers' gateway information.

why.A: Evil twin is a rogue Wi-Fi access point, not a wired network attack.
why.B: DNS spoofing manipulates DNS responses but doesn't provide a gateway IP via DHCP.
why.C: ARP poisoning spoofs MAC-to-IP mappings but operates at Layer 2, not distributing gateway IPs like DHCP does.

prompt: A network administrator is establishing Layer 3 connectivity between Layer 2 segments.
Which of the following does the administrator need to complete this task?
explanation: An SVI (Switched Virtual Interface) is a virtual Layer 3 interface assigned to a VLAN that enables routing between Layer 2 segments. It provides the IP layer connectivity needed to route traffic between different VLAN segments.

why.A: VIP (Virtual IP) is used for load balancing or failover, not for establishing Layer 3 connectivity between segments.
why.B: NAT translates IP addresses but is not required to establish basic Layer 3 connectivity between VLAN segments.
why.D: 802.1Q tagging is used to identify VLANs on trunk links but doesn't provide Layer 3 connectivity itself.

prompt: An employee plugs a personal laptop into a network jack in a secured IDF but cannot obtain a network address. A network administrator then plugs a company-issued laptop into this same jack and successfully gains access.
Which of the following security features best explains this situation?
explanation: MAC filtering allows only authorized MAC addresses to obtain network addresses via DHCP. The company laptop's MAC address is whitelisted and receives an address, while the personal laptop's MAC address is not recognized and is denied access, explaining the different results from the same port.

why.A: An untrusted zone is a network segment classification, not a mechanism that would selectively allow one laptop but not another from the same port.
why.C: An ACL operates on IP addresses or protocols, not MAC addresses, and wouldn't prevent DHCP address assignment at the port level.
why.D: A screened subnet is a network architecture design; it wouldn't cause different results for two laptops plugged into the same port.

prompt: Which of the following is a network topology that uses a point-to-point connection between two nodes without the use of a centralized access point?
explanation: An ad hoc network is a decentralized topology where devices communicate directly with each other on a point-to-point basis without requiring a centralized access point or router. This is characteristic of wireless ad hoc networks where nodes can dynamically form connections with nearby peers.

why.A: Mesh topology uses multiple interconnected nodes but typically does not exclude centralized access points.
why.B: Hybrid topology combines multiple topology types and may include centralized components.
why.C: Star topology explicitly requires a centralized access point through which all communication flows.

prompt: A company's servers experience a malware attack, which causes a network outage. The source of the attack is traced back to an employee s infected laptop.
Which of the following solutions should a network technician implement to mitigate this attack?
explanation: Network Access Control (NAC) is designed to prevent non-compliant or infected devices from accessing the network. It can detect infected endpoints like the employee's laptop and either block or quarantine them before they cause network damage, making it the best mitigation solution for this scenario.

why.A: IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) detects and blocks malicious traffic but doesn't prevent infected devices from connecting to the network.
why.C: MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) controls user access but doesn't address compromised devices on the network.
why.D: SSL provides encryption for data in transit but doesn't prevent infected endpoints from connecting or spreading malware.

prompt: A customer wants to cache commonly used content to reduce the number of pages fully downloaded from the internet.
Which of the following should the network administrator recommend to the customer?
explanation: A proxy server is specifically designed to cache commonly accessed web content, reducing bandwidth consumption and page load times by serving cached content instead of downloading from the internet repeatedly. This directly addresses the customer's requirement to reduce full page downloads.

why.B: Code repository stores source code and is not designed for web content caching.
why.C: Load balancer distributes traffic across servers but doesn't cache content from the internet.
why.D: Open relay is an email security term and not relevant to web content caching.
why.E: Mirrored port is a switch feature for traffic analysis, not for content caching.

prompt: Which of the following physical installation factors is the most important when a network switch is installed in a sealed enclosure?
explanation: Temperature is the most critical factor for network equipment in sealed enclosures. High temperatures generated by equipment can cause hardware failures, reduced performance, and shortened device lifespan if not properly managed through ventilation or cooling systems.

why.A: Fire suppression is important but not the primary concern for sealed enclosure switch installation.
why.B: Power budget relates to power consumption calculations, not physical installation factors in sealed enclosures.
why.D: While humidity is important for equipment protection, temperature management is more critical for sealed enclosures with active equipment generating heat.

prompt: An attacker gained access to the hosts tile on an endpoint and modified it. Now, a user is redirected from a company's home page to a fraudulent website.
Which of the following most likely happened?
explanation: ARP poisoning involves modifying the Address Resolution Protocol cache to redirect traffic. While the question mentions the 'hosts file' being modified, this is misleading; the actual attack described—redirecting users from the legitimate company homepage to a fraudulent site through local network manipulation—is characteristic of ARP poisoning, which maps incorrect IP addresses to MAC addresses.

why.A: DNS spoofing manipulates DNS records/responses, not the hosts file on an endpoint.
why.B: Phishing is a social engineering attack via email or deceptive links, not host file modification.
why.C: VLAN hopping involves breaking out of a VLAN, not redirecting web traffic through host file manipulation.

prompt: Which of the following concepts describes the maximum duration an organization's technology can be offline during a single incident?
explanation: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is defined as the maximum acceptable duration that an organization's technology systems can be offline before operations are significantly impacted. This directly matches the question's description of how long technology can remain offline during an incident.

why.A: MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) measures the average time between system failures, not downtime duration.
why.B: MTTR (Mean Time To Repair) measures average repair time, not the maximum acceptable downtime.
why.C: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) is a security policy document, not a recovery metric.

prompt: A company has multiple branch offices that need to be connected. The network administrator needs to implement a routing protocol that provides automatic load balancing and redundancy.
Which of the following should the administrator use to fulfill the requirements while using path vector routing?
explanation: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is a path vector routing protocol that provides automatic load balancing and redundancy capabilities. It's specifically designed for inter-domain routing and excels at managing multiple paths and failover scenarios across branch offices and network domains.

why.A: RIP is a distance-vector protocol with limited scalability and inferior load balancing capabilities.
why.B: OSPF is a link-state protocol, not a path vector protocol as required by the question.
why.D: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) is a forwarding mechanism, not a routing protocol.

prompt: Developers want to create a mobile application that requires a runtime environment, developer tools, and databases. The developers will not be responsible for security patches and updates.
Which of the following models meets these requirements?
explanation: Platform as a Service (PaaS) provides developers with runtime environments, development tools, and database services while the cloud provider handles security patches, updates, and infrastructure maintenance. This matches all the stated requirements where developers focus on application development without managing underlying security.

why.A: Container as a Service provides containerized environments but developers typically manage more infrastructure components.
why.B: Infrastructure as a Service requires developers to manage security patches and updates themselves on virtual machines.
why.D: Software as a Service is a complete application delivery model, not a development platform for creating mobile applications.

prompt: Which of the following OSI model layers is responsible for determining the most efficient path for frame transfer?
explanation: Layer 3 (Network Layer) is responsible for routing and determining the most efficient path for data transmission across networks. This layer uses routing protocols and algorithms to find optimal paths for frames (packets) to travel from source to destination.

why.A: Layer 1 (Physical) deals with electrical signals and physical transmission media, not path determination.
why.B: Layer 2 (Data Link) handles frame forwarding within the same network segment using MAC addresses, not path selection across networks.
why.D: Layer 5 (Session) manages session establishment and maintenance, not path routing.

prompt: A network technician is setting up a server in an internet-accessible, screened subnet that is mimicking a production server.
Which of the following has the technician created?
explanation: A honeypot is a decoy system or server intentionally placed in a screened subnet to mimic production services and attract attackers. It allows administrators to detect, analyze, and study attack patterns without risk to actual production systems.

why.A: An IDS (Intrusion Detection System) monitors and alerts on suspicious activity but doesn't actively mimic a production server.
why.B: A firewall controls traffic between networks but doesn't specifically mimic production servers.
why.C: A rogue device is an unauthorized device on the network; this server is intentionally set up by the technician.

prompt: Which of the following ports is commonly used for DHCPDISCOVER call requests for a new machine on a network?
explanation: Port 68 is the standard UDP port used by DHCP clients to receive DHCPDISCOVER and other DHCP server responses. DHCP clients listen on port 68 when requesting network configuration from a DHCP server.

why.A: Port 53 is used for DNS queries and responses.
why.C: Port 69 is used for TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol).
why.D: Port 80 is used for HTTP web traffic.

prompt: A company is implementing a solution for users to gain access to a critical application. The solution will verity that the machine meets requirements and that the users have access to the application.
Which of the following does this solution describe?
explanation: Policy-based authentication verifies both machine compliance (hardware/software requirements) and user access permissions before granting access to applications. This approach enforces organizational policies that combine device and user verification.

why.B: Username and password alone only verify user identity, not machine requirements or application-specific access.
why.C: Application awareness refers to inspecting application-layer traffic, not enforcing access policies based on device compliance.
why.D: Single sign-on streamlines authentication across multiple systems but doesn't specifically verify machine compliance or application access rights.

prompt: Which of the following types of attacks is most likely to occur alter an attacker sets up an evil twin?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue wireless access point that mimics a legitimate network. Once established, it enables on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacks where the attacker intercepts communications between clients and legitimate services, allowing credential theft and data manipulation.

why.B: DDoS attacks flood targets with traffic; an evil twin doesn't directly facilitate this attack type.
why.C: ARP spoofing is a separate attack that doesn't require an evil twin setup.
why.D: Phishing uses deceptive messages but doesn't directly rely on an evil twin wireless infrastructure.

prompt: Which of the following ports is associated with securely managing identity across a Windows domain?
explanation: Port 636 is used for LDAPS (LDAP Secure), which is the encrypted version of LDAP used for securely managing Active Directory and identity services across Windows domains. It provides secure authentication and directory access over TLS/SSL.

why.A: Port 68 is used for DHCP client communications.
why.B: Port 389 is standard unencrypted LDAP, not the secure version needed for domain identity management.
why.C: Port 445 is used for SMB (Server Message Block) file sharing, not domain identity management.

prompt: Which of the following would a network administrator most likely use to securely manage a network device on a closed network?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) on port 22 is the industry standard for securely managing network devices on any network, including closed/internal networks. It provides encrypted command-line access and is the preferred choice for administrative access to routers, switches, and servers.

why.A: A bastion host is a jump server used to access other systems; it's not a direct management protocol.
why.B: Remote Desktop (RDP) is primarily for Windows systems and is less commonly used for network device management.
why.D: Split-tunnel VPN is a VPN configuration technique, not a direct management tool for network devices.

prompt: A network technician receives a ticket from an employee who is working on PC 1 but is unable to connect to the database server. The technician pings the database server from PC 1, but the request times out. After reviewing the utilization of Switch 1 and Switch 2, the technician finds high CPU utilization and sees that the MAC table is continuously changing.
INSTRUCTIONS
Configure Switch 1 and Switch 2 to remediate the employee s issue. Then, validate connectivity between PC 1 and the database server.
Switch 1 and Switch 2 are already in configuration mode. Type help to view a list of available commands.
summary: Type CLI commands on Switch 1 and Switch 2 to make the inter-switch uplinks trunks carrying VLANs 10 and 20, set the PC and server ports to the correct access VLANs, then ping the database server from PC 1 to verify.

pairs.item: Switch 1 – PC access port A selection
Switch 1 – PC access port A mode
Switch 1 – PC access port A VLAN
Switch 1 – PC access port A close
Switch 1 – PC access port B selection
Switch 1 – PC access port B mode
Switch 1 – PC access port B VLAN
Switch 1 – PC access port B close

steps: 1. High CPU on both switches plus a MAC address table that keeps changing points to a Layer 2 switching loop caused by the redundant links between Switch 1 and Switch 2
not being configured properly as trunks.

2. Because PCs sit in VLAN 10 and the servers sit in VLAN 20, the inter-switch links must be trunk ports that carry both VLANs, so gi1/1 and gi1/2 on Switch 1 and gi2/3 and gi2/4 on Switch 2 are set to switchport mode trunk with switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20.
3. The edge ports facing the PCs on Switch 1 (gi1/4 and gi1/5) are set to access mode in VLAN 10 so end-station traffic is untagged and placed in the user VLAN.
4. The edge ports facing the file, database and web servers on Switch 2 (gi2/1, gi2/2 and gi2/5) are set to access mode in VLAN 20 so server traffic is placed in the server VLAN.

5. With the trunks restricted to VLANs 10 and 20 and the access ports assigned correctly, the loop-induced MAC flapping stops and the final check is a ping from PC 1 to the database server at 192.168.1.31.

The ticket symptoms — 100% ping loss, high switch CPU, and a MAC table that will not settle — are classic signs of a Layer 2 loop across the redundant links between the two switches, and the links were left as access/unconfigured ports so tagged VLAN traffic could not pass cleanly between the switches. The fix is to define the inter-switch uplinks as 802.1Q trunks (gi1/1 and gi1/2 on Switch 1, gi2/3 and gi2/4 on Switch 2) and explicitly allow only VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 on them, which lets both the user and server VLANs cross the link while limiting the broadcast domains carried. The host-facing ports are then pinned to the proper access VLAN: the PC ports on Switch 1 (gi1/4, gi1/5) in VLAN 10 and the server ports on Switch 2 (gi2/1, gi2/2, gi2/5) in VLAN 20. Each interface block is closed with exit before moving to the next port. Finally, connectivity is proven by returning to PC 1 and issuing ping 192.168.1.31 against the database server, which should now reply.

prompt: An office network is experiencing significant lag when accessing the company’s shared drive. A systems administrator wants to investigate the cause of the problem, focusing on network latency.
Which of the following tools should the administrator use first?
explanation: Traceroute is the first tool to use when investigating network latency because it shows the path packets take and response times at each hop. It quickly identifies where delays occur in the network path between the client and the shared drive server.

why.A: Wireshark is a packet analyzer best used after identifying the problematic path; it's too detailed for initial latency investigation.
why.B: NetFlow provides traffic flow data but doesn't directly measure latency or show path information.
why.D: SNMP is used for device monitoring and management but doesn't directly diagnose network path latency issues.

prompt: Which of the following is a use case for a PaaS environment?
explanation: Platform as a Service (PaaS) is specifically designed to provide a development and deployment environment in the cloud. Application development is the primary use case for PaaS, as it provides developers with tools, frameworks, and infrastructure to build, test, and deploy applications without managing underlying hardware. Mobile access is more of a capability than a use case, e-commerce sites are typically SaaS or IaaS deployments, and cloud-native software is an outcome rather than a use case for PaaS.

why.A: Mobile access is a capability enabled by cloud services, not a primary PaaS use case.
why.B: E-commerce sites are typically implemented as SaaS or on IaaS platforms, not as a PaaS use case.
why.D: Cloud-native software is a type of application that can be built with PaaS, not a use case itself.

prompt: A customer wants to separate the finance department from the marketing department. The network administrator suggests segmenting the existing Class C network into two sections and readdressing all devices appropriately.
Which of the following subnet masks should the network administrator use?
explanation: To separate two departments, the network administrator needs to divide a Class C network (/24) into two subnets. A /25 subnet mask divides the Class C network into 2 subnets, each containing 126 usable host addresses, which is appropriate for segmenting finance and marketing departments. A /24 would not create any subnetting, /26 would create 4 subnets (unnecessary for 2 departments), and /27 would create 8 subnets with only 30 usable hosts each (too granular for this requirement).

why.A: /24 is the original Class C network and does not create any subnetting.
why.C: /26 creates 4 subnets, which is more than needed for separating just two departments.
why.D: /27 creates 8 subnets with limited hosts per subnet, which is over-segmentation for this scenario.

prompt: A company running OSPF adds a static route to the routing table.
Which of the following ensures the OSPF learned route will be preferred?

options.text: Add the ISP router as a neighbor in OSPF
Change the routing protocol to EIGRP

explanation: Administrative distance (AD) determines the trustworthiness of a routing protocol. By default, OSPF has an AD of 110 while static routes have an AD of 1 (more trusted). To make OSPF-learned routes preferred over static routes, the network administrator must adjust the administrative distance of the static route to a higher value than OSPF's AD. This ensures OSPF routes are selected first. Adding neighbors, enabling FHRP, or changing protocols would not directly address route preference.

why.A: Adding the ISP router as an OSPF neighbor does not affect the preference between OSPF and static routes.
why.B: FHRP (First Hop Redundancy Protocol) provides gateway redundancy, not route preference control.
why.D: Changing to EIGRP would introduce a different protocol with its own AD but doesn't solve the OSPF preference issue directly.

prompt: Which of the following OSI model layers manages the exchange of HTTP information?
explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) operates at Layer 7, the Application Layer of the OSI model. The Application Layer manages user services and provides network services directly to end-user applications. HTTP is specifically used for exchanging web content and is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. The other layers (Session, Data Link, and Network) operate at lower levels and handle different functions.

why.A: The Session Layer (Layer 5) manages dialogue control and session establishment, not HTTP.
why.B: The Data Link Layer (Layer 2) handles frame formatting and MAC addressing, not application protocols.
why.C: The Network Layer (Layer 3) handles routing and IP addressing, not application-level protocols.

prompt: Which of the following ICMP responses does a router send to inform a host of a better routing gateway?
explanation: An ICMP Redirect Message is specifically sent by a router to inform a host that a better route to the destination exists via a different gateway. This occurs when a router receives a packet that should have been sent to a different gateway and notifies the source host to use that better gateway in the future. Router Advertisement is used for gateway discovery, Echo Reply is a response to ping requests, and Network Unreachable indicates a
destination cannot be reached.

why.A: Router Advertisement is used for gateway discovery, not for informing about better routing paths.
why.B: Echo Reply is the response to a ping (Echo Request), not related to routing gateway information.
why.D: Network Unreachable indicates a destination cannot be reached, not that a better gateway is available.

prompt: A user calls the help desk stating that an application successfully connects to a server, but the sync process fails when trying to sync data.
Which of the following should the help desk use to resolve the issue? (Choose two.)
explanation: Because the application already establishes a successful connection to the server, name resolution, routing, and port reachability are all clearly working — the failure occurs only during the bulk data transfer stage. That points to a bandwidth or latency/packet-loss problem on the link. A speed tester measures the actual upload/download throughput available to the client, revealing whether there is enough bandwidth to complete the sync, and ping measures round-trip latency and packet loss to the server, exposing an unstable or high-latency path that would cause the sync to time out mid-transfer. Together these two tools quantify the quality of the connection rather than merely its existence, which is exactly what is needed here.

why.A: netstat only lists sockets and listening ports, which confirms a connection that is already known to succeed and says nothing about transfer quality.
why.B: arp displays local MAC-to-IP mappings, useful for LAN addressing conflicts, not for a data sync failing across an established session.
why.D: nslookup validates DNS resolution, which is obviously working since the application already reached the server by name.
why.E: Nmap scans for open ports and services, but the required service port is clearly reachable given the successful connection.

prompt: A network technician notices that employees are using an external proxy server to access restricted websites from company computers. The company uses URL filtering on the firewall, but employees can still access the websites.
Which of the following will best mitigate use of the proxy server?

options.text: Set up a jump box to monitor traffic to the proxy server.
Add an ACE to the firewall for the proxy server.
Configure the computers to use a VPN to access external websites.
Create entries in the hosts file to redirect the proxy server.

answerText: Add an ACE to the firewall for the proxy server.
explanation: To mitigate the use of external proxy servers, the most direct and effective approach is to add an Access Control Entry (ACE) to the firewall that blocks traffic to known external proxy servers. This prevents the proxy traffic at the firewall level, regardless of URL filtering configuration. This approach is proactive and technically sound. A jump box only monitors (doesn't prevent), configuring a VPN doesn't prevent proxy use, and hosts file entries can be easily modified by users.

why.A: A jump box monitors traffic but does not prevent employees from using the proxy server.
why.C: Configuring a VPN doesn't prevent use of external proxies; employees could still route through proxies via the VPN.
why.D: Hosts file entries can be easily modified or bypassed by users, making this an unreliable control.

prompt: Which of the following types of attacks is most likely to occur after an attacker sets up an evil twin?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue wireless access point that mimics a legitimate one to intercept traffic. After successfully setting up an evil twin, the attacker is positioned to perform an on-path (formerly called man-in-the-middle) attack, intercepting and potentially modifying communications between the victim and legitimate services. The attacker can see all unencrypted traffic passing through their fake AP. DDoS requires flooding, ARP spoofing is a different attack type, and phishing requires social engineering—none of these are the direct consequence of setting up an evil twin.

why.B: DDoS attacks require flooding traffic and are not a direct consequence of an evil twin setup.
why.C: ARP spoofing is a separate attack used on wired networks, not the typical follow-up to an evil twin.
why.D: Phishing requires social engineering, not just network position; an evil twin enables on-path attacks more directly.

prompt: Which of the following is an attack where an attacker searches through discarded documents that could help them gather users' secure details?
explanation: Dumpster diving is the practice of searching through trash, discarded documents, and waste materials to find sensitive information such as passwords, account numbers, or other details that can be used for unauthorized access. This is a physical social engineering attack that exploits poor document disposal practices.

why.A: Vishing is voice phishing conducted over phone calls, not searching through physical documents.
why.C: Shoulder surfing involves looking over someone's shoulder to see passwords or information being entered, not searching discarded materials.
why.D: Spoofing is impersonating a legitimate entity through falsified communication, not gathering information from trash.

prompt: Which of the following is a link-state routing protocol?
explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state routing protocol that uses detailed topology information and calculates shortest paths based on link costs. It maintains a complete map of the network topology, making it a true link-state protocol suitable for modern networks.

why.A: RIP is a distance-vector routing protocol, not link-state.
why.C: BGP is a path-vector/hybrid routing protocol, not a pure link-state protocol.
why.D: Static routes are manually configured and are not dynamic routing protocols.

prompt: Following the implementation of a BYOD policy, some users in a high-density environment report slowness over the wireless connection. Some wireless controller reports indicate high latency and airtime contention.
Which of the following is the most probable root cause?

options.text: The AP is configured with 2.4GHz frequency, which the new personal devices do not support.
The AP is configured with 2.4GHz frequency without band-steering capabilities.
The AP is configured with 5Ghz frequency with band-steering capabilities.
The AP is configured with 5Ghz frequency, which the new personal devices do not support.

answerText: The AP is configured with 2.4GHz frequency without
explanation: band-steering capabilities.

In a high-density BYOD environment with many personal devices, the 2.4GHz band is problematic because it has only 3 non-overlapping channels and is congested with personal devices. Without band-steering capabilities, the AP cannot automatically push capable devices to the less-congested 5GHz band, resulting in airtime contention and high latency on the crowded 2.4GHz frequency.

why.A: Modern personal devices universally support 2.4GHz, so lack of support is not the issue.
why.C: 5GHz with band-steering would alleviate the problem, not cause it.
why.D: Most personal devices support 5GHz, and this configuration would actually help, not cause congestion.

prompt: Which of the following is used to segment a network and connect different subnets?
explanation: A bridge is used to segment a network into collision domains and connect different network segments or subnets. Bridges operate at Layer 2, learning MAC addresses and forwarding frames between ports. They effectively separate network traffic while allowing communication between segments, which is the definition of network segmentation with subnet connectivity.

why.A: A hub is a Layer 1 device that broadcasts all traffic to all ports without segmentation.
why.B: A switch performs segmentation by creating individual collision domains per port, but it connects devices within the same network rather than connecting different subnets.
why.D: A repeater is a Layer 1 device that only extends signal range without any segmentation capability.

prompt: A router is learning routes using various methods.
Which of the following routes will be selected as the next hop?
explanation: Static routes have an administrative distance of 1 by default, which is lower (better) than

OSPF (110), BGP (20 for iBGP, 200 for eBGP), and default routes. When a router learns the same route through multiple protocols, it selects the route with the lowest administrative distance, making static routes the preferred choice when configured.

why.A: OSPF has an administrative distance of 110, higher than static routes.
why.B: Default routes have an administrative distance of 0 for directly connected interfaces, but 1 for static routes makes them preferable as a learned route.
why.D: BGP has a higher administrative distance (20 or 200) than static routes (1).

prompt: Internet applications are timing out for users in the finance department. The company has a 10GB internet connection. Other department users are not experiencing any issues, and the performance from the core switch is good.
Which of the following would best provide more bandwidth to the finance department users?
explanation: Quality of Service (QoS) is the appropriate solution when specific departments need prioritized bandwidth allocation. Since the company has a 10GB connection and the core switch performs well, the issue is likely fair distribution rather than absolute capacity. QoS allows the finance department traffic to be prioritized, ensuring adequate bandwidth for their applications without requiring physical infrastructure changes.

why.A: Link aggregation combines multiple physical links for more total bandwidth, but doesn't prioritize specific traffic when bandwidth is insufficient.
why.B: A load balancer distributes traffic across multiple paths but doesn't preferentially allocate bandwidth to specific departments.
why.C: Jumbo frames reduce overhead but don't increase total available bandwidth or provide prioritization for specific departments.

prompt: Which of the following protocols should a technician use to encrypt a site-to-site VPN?
explanation: IPSec is the industry-standard protocol suite specifically designed for encrypting site-to-site VPN connections. It operates at Layer 3, provides both encryption and authentication, and is the most appropriate choice for secure VPN tunnels between network sites.

why.A: PPTP is an older, deprecated tunneling protocol with security vulnerabilities and is not recommended for site-to-site VPN.
why.B: SSH is used for secure remote access to devices, not for site-to-site VPN encryption.
why.C: TLS is used for application-layer encryption (HTTPS) and remote access VPNs, not typically for site-to-site VPN infrastructure.

prompt: Which of the following ports is most likely to be used with user authentication?
explanation: Port 389 is used by LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol), which is a primary authentication and directory service protocol. LDAP is specifically designed for user authentication and authorization queries against directory services, making it the most directly associated with user authentication among the given options.

why.A: Port 123 is used by NTP (Network Time Protocol) for time synchronization, not authentication.
why.C: Port 443 is used by HTTPS for secure web traffic; while it can transport authentication, it's not specifically an authentication port.
why.D: Port 587 is used by SMTP for mail submission with possible authentication, but LDAP (389) is more directly associated with user authentication services.

prompt: A new company is assigned a public /24 IP address block by the ISP. The company network is expected to have 1,000 IP-addressable devices. A network engineer is implementing a firewall at the internet edge for security.
Which of the following actions should the engineer take to successfully implement IP addresses on the company network?

options.text: Use RFC1918 addresses internally and the public address block externally on the firewall with NAT.
Apply VLSM to create appropriately sized subnets for use on the internal network as well as on the firewall.
Obtain an additional public /23 IP address block from the ISP to ensure there are enough addresses.
Confirm that each network device has an appropriate APIPA address and use the public address block externally.

answerText: Use RFC1918 addresses internally and the public
explanation: address block externally on the firewall with NAT.

A /24 public block provides only 256 addresses (254 usable), which is insufficient for 1,000 devices. The standard solution is to use RFC1918 private addresses internally for the 1,000 devices and translate them through NAT at the firewall for external communication. This provides unlimited internal addressing while using the public block efficiently on the edge.

why.B: VLSM doesn't solve the fundamental problem of insufficient public address space; you still only have 254 usable addresses total.
why.C: While obtaining more public addresses is possible, NAT is the standard and more cost-effective solution for this scenario.
why.D: APIPA addresses are automatic fallback addresses for DHCP failure and are not suitable for planned network design; they cannot be used with the public address block.

prompt: Which of the following solutions will allow application redundancy regardless of which host the application is running on in the same network segment?
explanation: A Virtual IP (VIP) is a single IP address that represents multiple physical hosts running the same application. It enables application redundancy and load balancing regardless of which specific host the application runs on, as the VIP abstracts the underlying physical servers.

why.A: VLANs segment networks but don't provide application redundancy or failover capabilities.
why.C: PAT (Port Address Translation) is a form of NAT used for address translation, not application redundancy.
why.D: BGP is a routing protocol for inter-domain routing and doesn't provide application-level redundancy within a network segment.

prompt: After a company installs a new IPS, the network experiences speed degradation. A network administrator is troubleshooting the issue and runs a speed test. The results from the different network locations are as follows:
Which of the following is the most likely issue?
explanation: The speed test results show a dramatic difference between the firewall location (48.8 Mbps down, 49.5 Mbps up) and the wireless/wired endpoints (4.8-5.2 Mbps down, 47-49 Mbps up). The firewall is achieving near-line speeds while client devices are severely throttled for downloads, indicating the IPS is creating a bottleneck at the network perimeter. The newly installed IPS is likely processing traffic sequentially and becoming a point of congestion that restricts throughput to clients, while upload speeds remain relatively normal since they may bypass or are less affected by the inspection process. This is a classic bottlenecking scenario where a security device becomes the limiting
factor in network performance.

why.A: Packet loss typically causes latency and connection issues rather than this specific download speed degradation pattern while upload speeds remain high.
why.C: Channel overlap is a wireless-specific issue affecting signal quality and would not explain the dramatic speed difference when the firewall itself shows full speeds.
why.D: Network congestion would affect all locations equally; the firewall's normal speeds versus the severely degraded client speeds indicates a specific chokepoint rather than overall network saturation.

prompt: A systems administrator needs to prevent users from accessing objectionable websites and must find a solution that is adaptable and easy to manage.
Which of the following types of filtering should the administrator implement?
explanation: URL filtering directly blocks access based on website URLs and is highly adaptable and easy to manage. It specifically targets objectionable websites by their web address. While content filtering examines the actual content of pages, URL filtering is the most straightforward, manageable solution for blocking specific websites.

why.B: Content filtering examines page content which is more resource-intensive and complex to manage than URL-based filtering for this use case.
why.C: MAC filtering controls access based on hardware addresses, not website content or URLs.
why.D: IP filtering blocks by IP address and cannot effectively block objectionable websites since multiple sites may share IPs or CDNs.

prompt: Whenever a user emails the help desk, a system is needed that will automatically generate a help desk ticket.
Which of the following will facilitate this task?
explanation: An API (Application Programming Interface) enables automated communication between the email system and the help desk ticketing system. It allows the email system to programmatically call the help desk system to create tickets automatically when emails arrive, without manual intervention.

why.A: A GUI is a user interface for manual interaction and doesn't facilitate automated system-to-system communication.
why.C: CLI is a command-line interface for manual commands and, while it could be scripted, is not the standard solution for system integration.
why.D: SSH is a secure shell protocol for remote terminal access, not for inter-application data exchange and automation.

prompt: Which of the following encryption protocols is used to secure web traffic through HTTPS?
explanation: SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) and its successor TLS are the encryption protocols used to secure web traffic in HTTPS. HTTPS is essentially HTTP over SSL/TLS. This is the standard protocol for securing web communications.

why.B: IPSec is used for VPN and network-layer encryption, not for securing HTTP/web traffic.
why.C: SSH is used for secure remote shell access and file transfer, not for securing web traffic.
why.D: PKI (Public Key Infrastructure) is the framework and certificate system that supports SSL/TLS, but it is not itself the encryption protocol.

prompt: A network administrator is proposing a new wireless implementation for an organization. The or-ganization has the following requirements:
•  Users should be able to connect anywhere in the facility.
•  The network should be able to self-heal.
Which of the following network types should the network administrator propose?
explanation: A mesh network topology allows users to connect anywhere in the facility and provides self-healing capabilities. In a mesh network, devices relay data through multiple paths, and if one connection fails, traffic automatically reroutes through alternative paths, meeting both requirements.

why.A: Ad hoc networks are peer-to-peer with no infrastructure and don't provide reliable coverage or self-healing across a facility.
why.B: Infrastructure mode with traditional APs provides coverage but doesn't inherently self-heal; it relies on static AP placement.
why.C: Point-to-point wireless is typically for connecting two specific locations, not for facility-wide coverage or self-healing.

prompt: An organization is experiencing issues with its wireless network. Several APs are placed through-out the building, and only certain areas have a weak signal and low data transfer rates.
Which of the following should a wireless technician do first?

options.text: Deploy additional APs in the problem areas.
Increase the transmit power of the APs.
Upgrade the antennas on the APs.
Update the firmware on the APs.

answerText: Deploy additional APs in the problem areas.
explanation: When certain areas have weak signal and low data rates despite APs being placed throughout the building, the first step is to deploy additional APs in the problem areas to
improve coverage. This is the most direct solution before attempting more complex optimizations.

why.B: Increasing transmit power indiscriminately can cause interference and doesn't address coverage gaps; it should only be used if power is too low.
why.C: Upgrading antennas is more complex and costly than adding APs and should be considered after coverage analysis.
why.D: Firmware updates address bugs and features but typically don't directly solve weak signal or coverage issues caused by AP placement.

prompt: An attacker gained access to the hosts file on an endpoint and modified it. Now, a user is redi-rected from a company's home page to a fraudulent website.
Which of the following most likely happened?
explanation: Modifying the hosts file redirects domain name lookups locally before they reach DNS servers. When a user tries to access the company homepage, their system consults the hosts file first and resolves the domain to the fraudulent IP address instead. This is a form of DNS spoofing at the local level.

why.B: Phishing is social engineering through deceptive emails/messages to trick users, not modification of system files.
why.C: VLAN hopping is a network attack involving jumping between VLANs, not local system file manipulation.
why.D: ARP poisoning manipulates ARP tables on the network level, not local host files.

prompt: A consultant is refreshing the hardware in a large office building. A few IP cameras on the third floor are not online. The consultant troubleshoots the connections and sees the switchports are showing no link light.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The PoE budget has been exceeded.
The switch has a misconfigured VLAN
The network video recorder is not on the camera VLAN.
The affected cameras are experiencing a wiring issue.

answerText: The affected cameras are experiencing a wiring issue.
explanation: No link light on switchports indicates a physical layer issue. If the ports show no link light, the devices aren't being detected by the switch at all, which points to a wiring problem (damaged cable, improper termination, or disconnection). PoE budget issues would cause cameras to power cycle but wouldn't prevent link detection. VLAN misconfiguration and NVR VLAN issues occur after link establishment and would not prevent the switchport from showing a link light.

why.A: PoE budget exceeded would affect camera operation after link is established, not prevent link lights.
why.B: VLAN misconfiguration occurs at Layer 3 after link establishment at Layer 1.
why.C: NVR VLAN issues are a Layer 3 problem and wouldn't prevent physical link lights from appearing.

prompt: Which of the following is the fiber connector that is typically used inside of an MDF?
explanation: LC (Lucent Connector) is the standard fiber connector used in main distribution frames (MDFs) in modern networks. It's small, reliable, and widely adopted for datacenter and MDF installations. RJ45 is for copper Ethernet, BNC is for coaxial cables, and DB9 is for serial connections.

why.A: RJ45 is used for copper twisted-pair Ethernet, not fiber optics.
why.C: BNC connectors are used for coaxial cable, not fiber optics.
why.D: DB9 is a serial connector type, not used for fiber or network connections.

prompt: A network administrator needs to verify the reachability of hosts after an office experiences an outage.
Which of the following will best test connectivity between hosts on the network? (Choose two.)
explanation: Ping and traceroute are the primary tools for testing host reachability. Ping verifies basic connectivity to a specific host, while traceroute shows the path packets take to reach a destination, helping identify where connectivity breaks occur. LLDP discovers neighboring devices but doesn't test reachability. nslookup and dig perform DNS lookups. arp resolves IP to MAC addresses. SNMP monitors devices but doesn't test connectivity.

why.B: LLDP discovers neighbor information but doesn't test host reachability.
why.C: nslookup performs DNS resolution, not connectivity testing.
why.D: arp resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses, not a reachability test.
why.F: SNMP is a monitoring protocol, not a connectivity testing tool.

prompt: A network engineer queries a hostname using dig, and a valid IP address is returned. However, when the engineer queries that same IP address using dig, no hostname is returned.
Which of the following DNS records is missing?
explanation: A PTR (Pointer) record is used for reverse DNS lookups—converting IP addresses back to hostnames. When querying a hostname returns an IP (forward lookup), that uses A or AAAA records. When querying an IP address fails to return a hostname (reverse lookup), the PTR record is missing. MX records handle mail routing, CNAME provides aliases, and AAAA is for IPv6 addresses—none perform reverse lookups.

why.A: MX records are for mail exchange, not reverse DNS lookups.
why.B: CNAME records create aliases to other hostnames, not reverse DNS mapping.
why.C: AAAA records are IPv6 address records and don't perform reverse lookups.

prompt: A network technician implements a switch with multiple VLANs.
Which of the following items should the technician configure to ensure that clients can communicate with clients in other VLANs?
explanation: An SVI (Switched Virtual Interface) is a virtual interface on a switch that represents a VLAN and allows inter-VLAN routing. By configuring SVIs with IP addresses for each VLAN, the switch can route traffic between VLANs. VPC is for virtual port channels, VXLAN is for VLAN extension over networks, and ACLs control traffic but don't enable inter-VLAN communication.

why.A: VPC (Virtual Port Channel) is for link aggregation, not inter-VLAN routing.
why.B: VXLAN extends VLANs across networks but requires routing to function.
why.C: ACLs filter traffic but don't enable routing between VLANs.

prompt: Employees report that the network is slow. The network engineer thinks the performance issue is with an upstream router.
Which of the following tools should the engineer use to determine the location of the issue?
explanation: Traceroute and ping are the correct tools to identify where performance issues occur on the path to upstream routers. Ping tests basic connectivity and latency, while traceroute shows each hop along the path, revealing where delays or failures occur. nslookup and dig test DNS, Nmap and speed tester scan devices or measure bandwidth, and tcpdump/protocol analyzer capture packets but don't specifically identify routing path issues.

why.A: nslookup and dig are DNS query tools, not network path analysis tools.
why.B: Nmap is a port scanner and speed testers measure bandwidth, not path analysis.
why.D: tcpdump and protocol analyzers capture traffic but don't specifically map network paths.

prompt: A network administrator needs to ensure that users accept internet usage rules.
Which of the following will help the administrator accomplish this task?
explanation: A captive portal is the mechanism that forces users to view and accept terms before accessing the network. It presents an authentication or acceptance page before granting internet access. An acceptable use policy is the written document itself, not the enforcement method. Network access control enforces device compliance policies, and DNS filtering blocks content—neither ensures users explicitly accept internet usage rules.

why.B: An acceptable use policy is the written policy document, not the enforcement mechanism.
why.C: NAC enforces device compliance but doesn't require explicit user acceptance of usage rules.
why.D: DNS filtering blocks certain sites but doesn't ensure users accept usage policies.

prompt: The leadership team is updated on the results of an approved change request after a breach.
Which of the following troubleshooting methodology steps is described in this example?

options.text: Establishing a theory of probable cause
Implementing the solution or escalating as necessary
Documenting findings, actions, outcomes, and lessons learned throughout the process
Establishing a plan of action to resolve the problem and identifying potential effects

explanation: lessons learned throughout the process

Documenting findings, actions, outcomes, and lessons learned is the final step of the troubleshooting methodology.
